## Source-read contract, before implementation

Pinned source commit: `66586c596e271408d9184af32eb31cd7218c126e` in the isolated
Elixir baseline. Read the actual reviewed architecture, ordered plan, parity
contract and prior type/domain/retry/claim review notes.

1. **Scope and admission.** Add distinct opaque binary `TenantId`, `GroupId`,
   `RecoveryId`, `RequestId` and `PartitionId` values under `wf-types::identity`.
   Constructors reject empty/oversize bytes, preserve binary equality/order,
   and keep existing RecordId/PartitionKey APIs stable. `workflow::admission`
   validates configured inline-value, encoded-key, total-command-byte and batch
   bounds before reducing. Applications supply actual committed key/value
   encodings; the domain does not manufacture source hashes/ETF bytes. Empty
   present payload/result/error remains different from omission. Bounds are
   configured immutable apply values, never local allocator conditions.
2. **Explicit committed envelope.** Add tenant/group/recovery/request scope,
   canonical client-intent digest/version, separate immutable prepared-entry
   digest, applied position and explicit time metadata under `workflow`.
   Application owns intent normalization/digest production. A private versioned
   committed codec belongs to outer preparation/storage; `wf-wire` owns public
   DTOs and intent mapping, never a durable command codec. Leader time, generated
   IDs/tokens and jitter must not enter the
   client-intent digest. The domain receives these values without clocks/random.
   Namespace and placement are checked against an authoritative borrowed view.
3. **Replay.** Look up the scoped request before current record/lease/revision
   guards. Equal intent returns the exact borrowed original retained result,
   with no workflow/index/history mutation; different intent rejects reuse.
   Recovery identity prevents replay across disaster restore. Retained outcome
   bytes are a versioned explicit adapter value, not recomputed from new state.
   Authorization before retained reads is an adapter obligation. The gate checks
   the immutable original expiry against deterministic effective execution time;
   cleanup/reachability remain adapter obligations. Legacy lease/fence duplicates
   remain in the existing reducer.
4. **Bounded same-group batches.** Borrow the unique current-record map and
   authoritative partition placement. Validate every member's placement,
   duplicate ID and input bounds before returning any plan; cross-group rejects.
   Preserve command order and produce only touched-record plans. A failed
   member returns a deterministic rejection with no partial plan. Source atomic
   bulk operations reject duplicate ID even across partitions. An app may later
   split independent cross-group bulk with ordered per-group outcomes.
5. **Policy definitions/install.** Add validated immutable type/state definition
   and retention/mode values, plus replace/patch install plans and expected
   generation. Public DSL installation defaults to replace; low-level explicit
   patch preserves unspecified type/state fields, supports state removal, and
   deeply merges supplied backoff fields before source normalization. Advance
   generation from max(stored, migration high-water) with the exact numeric
   ceiling. Policy bytes/digest preparation remains outside this module;
   no installed view implies storage persistence. Governance/indexed metadata
   fields need explicit supported/deferred decisions rather than silent loss.
6. **Time/replay models.** Add validated explicit HLC physical/logical and wall
   snapshot values. Commit/application time advancement is a separate plan from
   workflow eligibility time, with accepted/rejected/replayed and nonworkflow
   entry treatment frozen by coordinator ADR before implementation. Identical
   explicit inputs and authoritative state must yield equal plans, and new
   deterministic model tests exercise lease/fence/attempt/FIFO/request replay.

## TDD / review evidence

Contracts above were published before dependent source changes. Concrete review
findings, observed REDs and executed GREENs are recorded below. Tests added after
an implementation are expressly supplemental verification, not retroactive TDD.

## Canonical ordering/index contract before implementation

Root requested and accepted the API direction on 2026-10-09; architecture must
still independently review the actual implementation. Existing `reduce` and
record-only `decide_group_batch` remain compatible. A new `workflow::indexed`
wrapper will take the same bounded items plus an authoritative `ClaimRecord`
map, complete parallel/FIFO indexes and current `PolicySnapshot` mode views.
The caller supplies full `LogIdentity` and the first state-entry `u32` ordinal.
The canonical priority and exact `u128` sequence come from the current record
view, not candidate rows or client hints. Creation supplies admitted priority;
existing operations cannot change it through this reduced command surface.

`flow_create.ex:52,259-273,307-341` allocates
`u128(applied_index) * 2^32 + ordinal`; creation allocates even for terminal
records, and a changed nonterminal logical state allocates a new sequence.
Claims/reclaims and same-logical-state retries preserve it. Validate the first
and consumed ordinals without wrapping. `claim/index.rs` already preserves
running members in their logical lane and orders them before queued members.
Current mode comes from the coherent installed state policy; absent mode means
parallel. FIFO requires priority zero (`flow_create.ex:345-365`). Named claim
and reclaim must consume the real authoritative lane head; a canonical/index
mismatch is an apply failure, while a non-head command is a business guard
rejection. No complete lane follower scan is needed.

The output will own the existing touched-only `BatchPlan` and scalar ordering
metadata, borrowing predecessor records. Before/after semantic parallel due and
FIFO lane-member rows borrow predecessor/proposed record bytes; no copied key
or group/partition clone is introduced. A changed FIFO member identifies its
affected lane so M2 can update the lane/head/due authority atomically. No-op,
group rejection and exact log replay emit no index mutations or consumed
ordinals. This is a pure description, not physical key encoding or persistence.

## Reusable request gate contract before implementation

The committed request header will carry actual encoded isolation-scope bytes,
admitted independently at the source 8 KiB cap. Handle-length checks cannot
certify this composed encoding. An outer private decoder proves byte/typed-scope
binding; the domain checks actual slice lengths and complete opaque namespace
equality. A header-only gate borrows retained outcome authority and advances
control without consulting current record, policy, revision or index guards.
Fresh dispatch then calls the corresponding bounded reducer; retained/log replay
returns before that dispatch. This gate supports policy-generation and indexed
operations without representing them as a record mutation or fake service.
Retained policy errors use a validated business-only wrapper; operational
authority/preparation failures cannot enter retained status. Indexed guards
are likewise separate from apply failures. Existing record request behavior
remains available through `decide_request` composed over the gate.

Concrete fresh-only compositions are agreed with root before code:
`request::indexed::{IndexedRequestView, IndexedEnvelope, decide_indexed_request}`
combines gate authority, canonical indexed group authority and explicit first
ordinal; the sequence base comes from the header's complete log identity.
`request::policy::{PolicyRequestView, PolicyEnvelope, decide_policy_request}`
combines gate authority with stored/migration policy generation and explicitly
prepared policy bytes. Both return `DispatchPlan<T>` with fresh semantic result
or original replay/conflict/expiry/log replay. A private pure dispatch helper
calls only the owner's reducer on Fresh; no external callback/effect port is
public. Fresh malformed time/authority fails without a control plan. Fresh
business rejection retains a control plan and needs an outcome write. Original
replay and exact log replay contain no indexed/policy write or ordinal allocation.

## Genesis/restoration contract before implementation

Architecture/root independently read OpenRaft 0.9.25 `engine_impl.rs:199-209`,
`initialize_test.rs:34-55` and `storage/v2.rs:171-173`: initialization commits
membership at term/node/index zero and uses optional last-applied identity.
Root selected A-G1: `last_entry=None` is genuinely unapplied, and only first
index zero is admitted. The zero scoped position by itself proves no applied
entry. A restored control constructor derives checkpoint from full last-entry
identity and verifies its persisted HLC/wall dominate any stamped last entry.
Unapplied request authority cannot contain any retained outcome, even when the
requested key is absent. Existing new business fixtures retain positions by
explicitly applying real unstamped genesis zero before business one. Frozen
or assertion-linked historical counterparts are not changed.

## Implemented APIs and frozen resource decisions

`wf-types::identity` now exports distinct immutable opaque scope handles with
Vec constructor inputs and slice accessors. Tenant8,192, group/recovery/request256
and partition65,535 byte caps are **new selected profile decisions**, separate
from source complete isolation-scope8,192 and state-key65,535 encoded caps.
`version::{AppliedPosition, Revision, LogIdentity, HlcTimestamp, CommittedTime}`
retains checked counters, term/node/index identity, physical48/logical16 and
wall<=physical. A scoped index cannot prove a matching durable entry.

`workflow::admission::{AdmissionLimits, admit_command}` checks actual borrowed
key/value slices plus raw typed fields before copies. Inline default1MiB/hard
512MiB and item default1,000/hard100,000 are source ApplyLimits facts. Aggregate
default16MiB, at-most-two encoded single-record value occurrences, and
`4 * variable_bytes + 1,024 * touched_items` are **new selected represented
resource profiles**. Every multiplication/addition is checked; no native
`size_of`, capacity, allocator result or invented aggregate hard ceiling enters
a retained deterministic rejection. Actual encoded response admission is outer.

`workflow::batch::{GroupView, BatchItem, decide_group_batch}` borrows placement
and unique current records, rejects duplicate RecordId even across partitions,
and preserves input order. Only touched records/history/partition results are
owned. Current record and selected inherited retry exhaustion targets are
bounded before clones, including an intermediate target later overridden by
the command. An authoritative installed retry view for a touched policy retry
must match the canonical record's exact workflow type before state lookup/layer
work; a foreign type is ApplyError. Standalone legacy reduce/resolve keeps its
existing DomainError::PolicyTypeMismatch behavior. A late business guard exposes
no partial plan. Missing/conflicting authority and fallible vector reservation
are ApplyError, never retained status.

`workflow::control::{ControlState, plan_control}` implements actual ADR-004.
Unapplied `None` admits first0; restored checkpoints derive position from full
identity and require persisted clocks dominate their stamped last entry.
Checked consecutive indices, full identity/digest/stamp replay, term regression
and u64 exhaustion are distinct. Stamped entries use max lexical HLC plus max
wall; execution time is **HLC physical**, wall is separate. Unstamped consensus
entries preserve clocks. Exact last log replay preserves the entire control.

`workflow::request::gate::inspect_request` checks namespace/actual encoded scope,
required stamp and control before current operation guards. No outcomes are
valid in genuinely unapplied authority. Equal intent borrows the original
versioned response/status/full log identity/time/expiry without renewal;
changed intent and expired retention preserve the original. Record, indexed
and policy fresh-only compositions return no control plan on operational error;
fresh accepted/business-rejected entries require an original outcome write.
There is no public effect callback. An `EntryStamp::Unstamped` cannot populate
the required `CommittedTime` header; a compile-fail doctest exercises this.

`workflow::indexed` uses canonical priority/sequence, coherent policy mode and
complete borrowed correctness indexes. Log-index*2^32+checked ordinal allocates
on create or a changed nonterminal logical state. Claim/reclaim/same-state retry
and legacy no-op preserve sequence; rejected/replayed requests expose no new
ordinal/index plan. Borrowed semantic before/after rows do not encode physical
keys. FIFO head and touched entry bind both canonical record views with full
equality; exact overlapping parallel due authority fails. Bounded lookup replaces
whole-group/lane clones. M2 must atomically update affected lane/head/due rows.

`policy::{definition, installation}` and `retention` represent partial type/state
retry, retention, mode, max_active_ms, version, definition initial state and
install intent. Low-level default is Patch; definition default is Replace.
Patch preserves omitted fields, clears explicitly selected fields, deeply
merges backoff and deletes selected states. Generation is
max(stored,migration)+1 up to9,007,199,254,740,991, with expected-generation guard.
Installed/patch/final cardinality and raw selected strings validate before copy;
remove-before-add keeps candidate cardinality within admitted old/final counts.
Actual encoded snapshot<=256KiB, envelope<=snapshot-cap+1,024 and snapshot
batch<=4MiB are separate source constraints. Default max_states16,384/max262,144
and snapshot occurrence count100,000 are **new bounded-work profiles**, not
literal source defaults or one-snapshot-per-command claims. Outer encoding must
prove actual typed-byte correspondence; arbitrary fixture slices do not.

### Current concrete M1 gaps

1. Apply-selected claiming is missing. claim::select returns borrowed identities,
   actions and work/cursor metadata; it mints no lease, fence, record, history or
   index plan. workflow/request dispatch wraps indexed named batches and policy
   installation only. There is no decide_claim_selection or equivalent claim
   wrapper anywhere in current src. A preliminary conversational recollection of
   such a wrapper was corrected directly to root, architecture and performance
   after the actual source search. PreparedOperation has only Batch and
   InstallPolicy. A leader-chosen explicit named Claim/Reclaim is a separate
   represented contract and cannot substitute for authoritative query selection.
2. Source claim lifecycle is wider than current records. Creation freezes
   max_active_ms, per-record retention and history settings; current
   WorkflowRecord represents none of these. Source claim scans can fail an
   expired head or follower without returning a claim. A current policy's
   max_active_ms cannot stand in for the absent immutable per-record value.
   Pure creation/lifecycle/timeout plans are required before complete source
   claim acceptance; physical values, retention indexes and atomic durable
   writes belong to M2, with child propagation/governance breadth still M5.
3. Remaining represented-operation fields require an exact source registry.
   Current Create always returns AlreadyExists for an existing identity and has
   no source idempotent creation comparison; Transition cannot express source
   priority changes; ordinary create plus named claim does not express the
   create-and-claim compound contract. Source inline payload/result/error
   presence, customer guards, policy-default resolution, same-group compound
   work and explicit larger value/count profiles need assertion-level coverage.
   Missing attrs/state_meta/lineage/governance/effect/schedule/signal semantics
   remain included breadth obligations, rather than implicitly accepted fields.
4. Scope/time/request contracts exist for the current two prepared operations,
   but are not complete operation/profile acceptance. Typed canonical intent has
   one policy-set helper, not the complete workflow operation registry. Batch
   order, explicit guards, opaque values and caller time/deadline options need
   their own normalization/source controls. Generated stamp/token/IDs/jitter,
   log identity, prepared digest and live policy remain excluded from client
   intent. Private prepared encoding is a different identity. Outer bulk routing,
   ordered per-group outcomes, independent mode and sequential repeated-record
   pipelines must freeze their separate semantics before runtime implementation.
5. Current FIFO-selection and lease/fence models are meaningful but separate.
   There is no integrated query-selection/write/index/request-replay model.
   Apply-selected phases need deterministic byte/position/time, fresh/replay/
   empty, stale fence, reclaim, malformed consumed authority and bounded-work
   controls through one pure result. Source scenario/profile counterparts and
   the mandatory full case/assertion catalog remain independent gates. The old
   37 declarations/38 mappings/124 links are not promoted by this audit.

  physical states, optional priority, borrowed worker, lease_ms, limit),

  max_work_bytes. Exact API: Default selects128*1024*1024; new(u64) returns
  Result<Self,AdmissionError>, rejecting zero with existing InvalidLimits;
  max_work_bytes() reads the value. The trusted apply owner supplies this

  SelectionContinuation. This

Exact proposed ClaimRejection variants are InvalidScope, InvalidPriority,
InvalidBudget, HeadBudget, StaleContinuation, EmptyType, EmptyWorker, ZeroLease,
LeaseTooLarge, LeaseDeadlineTooLarge, VersionOverflow, FenceOverflow,
ValueTooLarge {bytes:usize,maximum:usize}, DecisionBytes, LengthOverflow and
WorkBytes {bytes:u64,maximum:u64}. They classify query/component/budget failures,
generated-token length, valid-lease arithmetic and checked counter exhaustion.
There is no InvalidAuthority, AllocationFailed, NotFifoHead, generic index/
selection/domain wrapper or invalid trusted-profile variant. InvalidLimits from
ClaimWorkLimits::new is constructor failure, not a retained outcome. The fresh
dispatcher maps corrupt consumed row priority/mode/type/placement, duplicate
scoped identity, missing/conflicting maps or encoding, unsupported committed
token version and allocation failure to ApplyError. The selected composition
also maps NotFifoHead/FifoPriority/InvalidPriority or a named-batch CrossGroup/
DuplicateId result to InvalidAuthority: these cannot be legitimate client
guards after coherent authoritative query selection. Current public named
batch rejection classifications remain intact. A supposedly selected candidate
which reduces to NotEligible/no write instead of Changed plus write/history is
an authority/composition failure; discard the whole phase. Only the explicitly
listed claim domain/arithmetic failures become a retained ClaimRejected.

The exact borrowed view binds consumed heads/rows to BOTH canonical record maps,
canonical policy mode and priority, authoritative partition placement, actual
key owners and the correct due/FIFO occurrence. A FIFO occurrence cannot also
exist in parallel; missing/stale/conflicting consumed authority is ApplyError,
not an empty/NotEligible business result. Complete relevant replicated index
authority is a view obligation, never a leader candidate window. Do not scan or
clone the full group to prove it. Unconsumed global completeness/corruption
verification remains the future adapter's restore/apply duty.

Request inspect precedes query filters, token derivation, policy/index/record
guards and output construction. Fresh only derives effective time from the
control plan, validates the immutable profile, selects and creates the full
plan. An accepted empty phase has no IndexedBatchPlan but finalizes this request
ID and requires an outcome write; polling/continuing uses a fresh ID. Retained
replay returns original bytes/time/position/retention and creates no new leases,
fences/history/index deltas/ordinals; an exact full log replay changes nothing.
Operational failure exposes no control plan. Fresh deterministic rejection may
persist control and rejection. Whole-phase failure exposes no partial writes.

Continuation proposal is deliberately snapshot-specific. A zero-write bounded
scan may resume only against the same full tenant/group/recovery scope, index
revision, complete ClaimQuery, token version, eligibility time, scan/head budgets
and effective separately supplied AdmissionLimits/ClaimWorkLimits values.
The new opaque wrapper retains those fields privately: SelectionContinuation
alone binds only its legacy logical SelectionRequest and cannot certify these
new semantics. Guard the wrapper first, then let the underlying cursor check
its exact mapped request/revision. A write invalidates that cursor: continue with a
fresh ID/query from current authority, without skipping its FIFO head. Count
or scan exhaustion stays distinct from completed empty eligibility. These are
private M1 planning semantics; a durable client/codec cursor must receive a
separate exact owner/format approval, not serialize private memory or be invented
under this batch. If architecture requires one persistent cursor for both cases,
it must choose its post-write revision/time binding before approving the model.

Resource proposal: retain the existing explicit initial max1000 selections,
16384 scans,4096 head reads and64 filter-footprint profile for this increment;
the inherited1024-byte selector component contract is also an explicit partial
profile. Larger source-compatible count/component profiles remain mandatory
unclosed work; this phase cannot certify them or label source-valid larger
records corrupt by definition. Count gates
precede loops/reserves. Query individual-length and Q-prefix admission precede
duplicate/filter/cursor comparisons. Bound each consumed canonical record and
name before full equality, including blocked/excluded/unselected lane heads.
Use checked sums/products and checked conversions between usize lengths and
the u64 work profile. The revised exact represented charge has two parts:

- Q sums actual query type/worker/physical-state/exclusion/partition bytes. For
  selected i, B_i is record_bytes(current)+record-ID length+expected physical
  state length+typed partition length+actual state-key length+worker length+
  precomputed source-token length. F_i is zero for parallel; for selected FIFO
  it is R(head.record)+R(GroupView head canonical), where R is the unchanged
  record_bytes result over each actual borrowed owner. F_i equals2*R only after
  coherence is established. P=4*(Q+sum B_i+sum F_i)+1024*selected. Check P against
  AdmissionLimits.decision_bytes, and separately check encoded_entry.len()
  against that profile, before token/command/partition/record/history ownership.
  This predicts the unchanged inner indexed gate
  4*(sum B_i+sum F_i)+1024*selected, including validate_head's two additional
  FIFO record occurrences. Two1MiB FIFO payloads contribute over24MiB to that
  inner gate, not8MiB. Do not weaken it or its non-touched-head validation.
  The B_i multiplier covers stage/final ID and token, stage/final/history
  worker, stage expected state, one record clone and logical-state replacement,
  and one owned partition. No extra command/token/partition clone is permitted
  by this ownership proof. Running bytes and history event-ID decimal text
  (at most37 bytes) fit the stable1024/item charge; index deltas borrow bytes.
- For each consumed head/parallel validation e, use actual R_entry, matching
  RecordIndex R_index and GroupView R_group lengths. The two guard comparisons
  plus existing selector validate_record compare entry/index, entry/group and
  entry/index: D_e=3*R_entry+2*R_index+R_group. Check this prefix before those
  full-value equalities. A head validated by read_heads is not revalidated merely
  because it is later merged; if an implementation repeats the guard/validation,
  it must add that actual occurrence. Even unselected heads receive D_e and
  name/scalar charges. Empty-lane metadata still counts as a head read.
- For selected i, anticipate the unchanged indexed equalities before staging:
  T_i=2*(R_entry+R_group)+(R_entry+R_member), plus
  (R_head+R_headIndex)+(R_head+R_headGroup) for FIFO. These are current during
  validation and final ordering, exact parallel/FIFO member, and the two FIFO
  head canonical comparisons. Missing members/maps are operational errors;
  inspect actual lengths before comparing, never assume equal payload sizes.
  With coherent equal values, D_e contributes6*R; T_i contributes6*R parallel
  or10*R FIFO. Thus selected parallel has six potential full-value Eq calls,
  selected FIFO eight, including exactly two new guard calls. Metadata/key
  equality adds no full record Eq; adding any such Eq requires revising proof.
- N sums query component names plus consumed ID/type/physical/logical-state/
  partition names and lane metadata actually read. G=encoded_entry.len()+
  sum D_e+sum T_i+256*N+1024*(head_reads+scanned). The256 term estimates bounded
  component validation/filter work, not intermediate BTree lookup keys or sort
  prefix comparisons. Count-bounded vectors/sets do not establish a strict CPU,
  comparator-byte, allocator-capacity or RSS bound. P+G must not exceed the
  separately supplied ClaimWorkLimits.max_work_bytes. Prefix G/Q checks happen
  before query/authority comparisons; complete P/G is checked before ownership.

The proposed128MiB work default is a new replicated admission profile, not a
source default or measured capacity; its selection still needs architecture/
root approval. The old16*A formula is withdrawn: three1MiB parallel payloads
formerly contributed at least156MiB including P. Under the read-occurrence
formula their payload contribution is36MiB to G plus12MiB to P, before names,
entry/scalar overhead. This corrected arithmetic is not an executable resource
or performance observation. Some source-valid workloads can still exceed the
new work or unchanged16MiB plan defaults. Every required source scenario must
receive sufficiently large immutable profiles, never omitted assertions or
client-controlled limits; zero/u64 overflow and exact/extra boundaries are
explicit tests. Unsupported larger scan/selection/filter profiles remain open.

Aggregate profile excess is a deterministic ClaimRejection of the whole phase,
with no partial leases; malformed individual authoritative values remain
ApplyError. Full equality and all canonical checks are retained. Performance

The current private ClaimPhase is one physical-state selection/mutation leaf.
Its Any/Only filters, server scan/head hints, token version and committed stamp
cannot be serialized wholesale as public caller intent. Public source behavior
adds the following responsibilities:

- ClaimDueAPI.ex93–153 validates/normalizes options before binding scope, then
  validates actual scoped key lengths before routing and checks returned scope
  before hydration. A typed normalizer cannot certify those keys or authority.
- ex1160–1284: omitted states or states:nil mean Any; explicit empty list
  rejects. Repeated/scalar states normalize with ASCII ANY recognition, mixed
  ANY+explicit rejects, and duplicate names retain their LAST occurrence/order.
  queued,ready,queued becomes ready,queued, not a sorted set.
- ex1034–1091: omitted/null scalar partition means Auto. Auto, Any, Global and
  explicit names are distinct. Scalar reserved aliases differ from list names;
  list duplicates retain their FIRST occurrence. Explicit empty list rejects.
  Source shared tenancy also rejects Any: SharedScopeTest586–642 requires the
  scope error, while explicit and auto claims preserve logical partitions and
  hide metadata. A normalized Any value is representable, not authorized.
- ex30–35/960–1019: fixed defaults are lease30,000, limit1, reclaim=true,
  ratio25 and priority omitted (drain2,1,0). Max claim limit is CONFIGURED,
  default1,000. SDK defaults such as60,000/32,000 are supplied explicitly by
  that caller/definition; do not resolve today's definition on a retry.
- PayloadReturn.ex9–53 and ClaimDueAPI.ex1001–1019: reply defaults Records,
  payload defaults to Records, full changes that default and payload overrides
  full. Payload cap absence depends on configured policy (source default65,536)
  and must stay absent in comparison. Named values omitted, all and empty differ;
  false equals an explicit empty name list, name dedup keeps FIRST/order.
- ex449–490: ordinary limit1 tries normal work BEFORE expired running, then
  running only if normal is empty. Larger limits first reclaim
  max(1,ceil(limit*ratio/100)), then normal remaining, then running remaining;
  replies concatenate phase order. Explicit running bypasses ratio/reclaim flag;
  reclaim=false removes running from normal, and ratio0 uses the ORIGINAL filter.
  PipelineClaimDue.ex261–307 instead sums per-call ceil running quotas, including
  limit1. Ordinary and coalesced pipeline calls are distinct contracts.
- Router.part_07.ex116–187/294–425/898–1188 coordinates Auto/Any/priorities,
  shard rotation and explicit-partition group quotas. Auto is not leaf Any and
  not a fabricated user Only list of256 buckets. Auto generation uses
  Keys.ex882–908 crc32%256, with canonical bucket/scoped matching. Cross-group
  calls are ordered independent effects, not an atomic group transaction.

**Selected smallest complete operation.** Propose `expire_active_batch`: given a
bounded ordered set of explicit scoped roots in one coherent group and trusted
effective apply time, expire every currently overdue root and finish its entire
same-group cancellation/parent-accounting closure before returning one plan.
This operation neither selects public CLAIM phases nor performs terminal GC.
It includes the canonical lifecycle authority needed to make that operation
complete, rather than accepting an eligibility boolean or calling worker Fail.
The future public parent derives its timeout root union at apply, gates its ID
once, and composes this private operation with claims in the SAME overlay/budget.
A leader-supplied candidate list is not public claim-selection authority.

**Actual source contract at66586c5.** Paths below abbreviate
`apps/ferricstore/lib/ferricstore/raft/state_machine/sections/`.

- `flow_create.ex258–293,580–605` captures resolved retention and max-active at
  creation. `flow/retry_policy.ex210–242,748–854` resolves max-active command
  integer first, explicit infinity to absent, then type policy; no state active
  override. Retention merges configured defaults/type/state/command, then clamps
  complete/hot history counts. Existing policy snapshot resolves only PUBLIC
  retention defaults/type/state; it lacks command capture and internal hot caps.
- `flow_retention_state.ex469–541` tests nonterminal `created_at+captured_max<=now`
  and reloads a pending put/delete before old canonical storage. Today's installed
  policy NEVER changes an existing captured deadline. Missing, already terminal,
  infinity and not-yet-expired roots have no timeout mutation/count.
- `flow_retention_state.ex543–585` increments version, fails, clears transient
  TTL/lease owner/token/deadline/next time, writes structured error
  `{reason:"max_active_ms",max_active_ms:d}` at the NEW versioned value identity,
  stamps terminal retention, moves indexes, writes state and a failed history
  event with both reason/duration, then cancels children and notifies parents.
  Fence, attempts, creation time, run-state and unrelated values are preserved.
- `flow_terminal.ex388–436,439–658,708–844` may recursively cancel descendants,
  update a parent's child status/result refs/summary, resolve ANY/ALL, change
  parent state, clear lease/TTL/next on resolution and notify terminal ancestors.
  Cancel-children marks group members/results even if a child is missing/already
  terminal; actual child mutation skips missing/terminal records. It may add a
  SECOND parent version/history event `children_cancelled` after `child_failed`.
  Missing parent or no open matching group is a source no-op, not fabricated
  failure. An open child is counted once. ALL+ignore resolves success when all
  children are terminal even when all failed; ANY+ignore fails only after all
  terminal with no completion; fail_parent resolves failure immediately. Internal
  child cancellation recurses into its descendants but NEVER notifies its own
  parent; the cancelling group's separate parent write accounts for those
  cancellations. Normal wait=None groups begin resolved=success with running

**Canonical values and exact proposed API.** Keep legacy `WorkflowRecord` and
named Claim/Reclaim/Terminal APIs stable. Its current251-line core lacks captured
lifecycle, refs and child accounting; `lineage.rs` is only a three-line reserved
boundary. `PolicySnapshotData` restores policies, not records. Propose a sealed
`ActiveRecord` aggregate owning the core, ordering and lifecycle data in ONE
canonical owner. Index/core maps are projections of that same value, validated
on every consumed identity. Independently supplied projection hints cannot
construct apply authority. A pure restoration constructor validates logical
values and moves owners; it provides no snapshot/disk/encoded provenance.

1. `WorkflowRecordData` names the existing core fields id/workflow_type/state/
   version/fence/attempts/created_at/updated_at/next_run_at/run_state/lease/payload/
   result/error plus the FULL latest witness `latest_kind:EventKind`,
   `latest_version:u64`, `latest_fence:Fence`. `restore_record(data,limits)` moves
   them after existing numeric/name/lease/value checks. It builds private
   LatestEvent from all three explicit fields; it never derives witness
   version/fence from the current record or EventKind. Its event witness is
   explicitly supplied by a future authoritative decoder, not inferred from
   state or accepted as proof of historical storage. This is needed to represent
   a nonterminal unscheduled parent without an artificial transition or setter.
   Add exact WorkflowStatus::Unscheduled and return it for a nonterminal unleased
   record with next=None; Scheduled continues to mean next=Some. Existing reachable
   legacy records retain their category. Running remains the PHYSICAL running
   label and may be restored with no lease/next, as source spawn/resolution
   targets admit that exact binary label and clear those fields. Validate any
   supplied Lease itself; do not derive required lease presence from state.
   Terminal categories are unchanged. This is a proposed restoration extension,
   not an inferred reinterpretation of Scheduled's existing deadline docs.
2. `MaxActiveOverride::{Inherit,Infinite,Millis(u64)}` preserves command absence
   versus opt-out. `LifecycleDefaults` has ttl_ms/history_hot_max_events/
   history_max_events/max_history_hot_max_events/max_history_max_events.
   `LifecycleOverrides` stores active:MaxActiveOverride,retention:RetentionOverride,
   history_hot_max_events:Option<u64>; this internal command field is not a public
   policy retention field. `capture_lifecycle(policy:Option<&PolicySnapshot>,workflow_type:&[u8],
   initial_state:&[u8],overrides:LifecycleOverrides,
   defaults:LifecycleDefaults)->Result<CapturedLifecycle,ActiveValueError>`
   borrows layers, verifies type equality and resolves before ownership.
   `CapturedLifecycle` stores max_active_ms:Option<u64>,retention_ttl_ms:u64,
   history_hot_max_events:u32,history_max_events:u32. Existing-record apply uses
   ONLY these captured values. Hot0/default0 is valid; complete history is positive.
   Command hot is clamped by trusted apply caps after precedence, including a
   larger command admitted by a source-compatible outer profile. If command hot
   and complete caps are BOTH supplied, preserve source hot<=complete validation
   before the clamp. Active deadline is exact created+captured duration, never
   clamped to MAX_EXACT; terminal retention is
   min(max(requested_now,trusted_apply_now)+ttl,MAX_EXACT). This predecessor takes
   trusted effective now for both inputs, granting no caller clock authority.
   No installer edit or live policy substitution.
3. `ActiveRecordData` owns core:WorkflowRecord,partition:PartitionId,
   ordering:OrderingMetadata,captured:CapturedLifecycle,ttl_ms:Option<u64>,
   terminal_retention_until:Option<TimestampMillis>,parent:Option<ParentLink>,
   root_id:Option<Vec<u8>>,correlation_id:Option<Vec<u8>>,child_groups:
   BTreeMap<Vec<u8>,ChildGroup>,values:ActiveValueRefs,carry:ActiveCarry,
   governance:Option<GovernanceReservation>. `restore_active(data,limits)` moves
   fields into sealed ActiveRecord after full count/byte/scalar validation.
   It admits absence/empty source metadata explicitly; never invents a parent.
4. `ParentLink` contains id:Vec<u8>,partition:Option<PartitionId>; absent parent
   partition falls back to child's partition. `ChildGroup` contains
   wait:ChildWait(None/All/Any),on_child_failed:ChildFailure(Ignore/FailParent),
   on_parent_closed:ParentClosed(Abandon/Cancel),success_state/failure_state:
   Vec<u8>,request_hash:Vec<u8>,children:BTreeMap<RecordId,ChildMember>,
   summary:ChildSummary(total/completed/failed/cancelled:u64),resolved:
   Option<ChildResolution(Success/Failure)>. `ChildMember` stores partition:
   Option<PartitionId>,status:ChildStatus(Running/Completed/Failed/Cancelled),
   result:Option<ChildResult>; ChildResult keeps status and optional result/error
   refs. Group-id/hash are captured opaque bytes; no domain hash/ETF generation.
   Constructors validate summary/internal results and unique keys WITHIN a group;
   they do not equate every old closed-group status to today's child state.
   Resolved success does NOT imply all children terminal: source wait=None starts

   Absent and explicitly empty parent/root/correlation bytes remain representable;

5. `ActiveValueRef::{Opaque(Vec<u8>),Versioned{partition:PartitionId,id:RecordId,

6. `GovernanceReservation` stores scope:Vec<u8>,shard_id:u64,reservation_id:Vec<u8>,

Use explicit `ActiveValueError` for pure restoration/capture invalid values;
fresh corrupt canonical/restored/index/history/outbox authority is
ApplyError::InvalidAuthority. Missing lookup is allowed ONLY when the complete
view proves canonical absence; a truncated loaded relation view is not absence.
Cross-group REQUEST roots return ActiveTimeoutRejection::CrossGroup; a foreign
dependency inside allegedly coherent same-group lineage is an operational
authority failure. The later SPAWN admission must keep exact source CROSSSLOT
business rejection before installing such a dependency. No cross-group partial
timeout/deferred parent update is exposed by this initial operation.

Proposed fresh-only signature:

```text
expire_active_batch<'view>(
  view: ActiveTimeoutView<'view>, roots:&[ScopedRecordId<'_>],
  now:TimestampMillis, order:EntryOrder, limits:AdmissionLimits,
  work:TimeoutLimits
) -> Result<ActiveTimeoutDecision<'view>,ApplyError>
```

The roots object's short lifetime is NOT returned. Ordered root occurrence is
preserved; duplicate scoped roots reload the overlay and timeout at most once.
Different partitions with the same ID remain distinct. `ActiveTimeoutView`
borrows IndexedGroupView, complete scoped ActiveRecord map, complete relevant
history-key maps and lifecycle-index authority, ReleaseOutboxState and shard
identity. It carries no policy max-active hint. `HistoryKey<'a>` is an explicit
ordered (event_ms:TimestampMillis,event_id:&'a[u8]) value: tie ordering uses actual
binary ID, not assumed numeric version order. `ActiveIndexKey<'a>` names only
ActiveTimeout/TerminalRetention/Due/DueAny/State/Inflight/Worker/Parent/Root/Correlation
semantic dimensions plus scoped identity; the borrowed BTreeMap value is its
actual scalar score. Due/FIFO authority uses the existing coherent index view.

`ActiveTimeoutDecision::{Accepted(ActiveTimeoutPlan<'view>),Rejected(ActiveTimeoutRejection)}`
has no partial plan. The plan owns final touched ActiveRecord writes, each with
ORIGINAL expected version, all intermediate `ActiveHistory` snapshots, new typed
timeout value writes, history trim/hot eviction descriptions, semantic index
changes and release-outbox appends/next metadata. Result stats count actually
expired roots, not child cancellations or skipped later roots. EventKind gains
only ChildCompleted/ChildFailed/ChildCancelled/ChildrenCancelled for generated
closure events and ChildrenSpawned as the required INPUT witness of an original
successful spawn (flow_create.ex76–97,563–577); no spawn reducer is added here.
The existing history fields/legacy witnesses remain stable. ActiveHistory adds
the missing source snapshot/ref/metadata fields without cloning a full record
or a child-group map for every event. After-key descriptions borrow final owners;
before/deletion keys borrow original authority and must stay alive through encode.
`ActiveTimeoutRejection` has exactly Admission(AdmissionError),Domain(DomainError),
CrossGroup,WorkBytes{bytes:u64,maximum:u64},Visits/Steps/Links/HistoryDeletes each
{count:u64,maximum:u64}, and ReleaseBacklog. ReleaseBacklog retains the source
`ERR flow governance release outbox backlog is full` business text; corrupt
metadata/tail/ownership are operational. No RetainedStatus variant is added by
this fresh-only predecessor; a later parent must approve its exact rejection
mapping rather than force an operational failure into retained business status.

Private `TimeoutTrace`/`ShadowRecord`/`ShadowGroup` are bounded scalar/reference
overlays, not cloned ActiveRecords. Trace depth/order matches source: fail root,
cancel its descendants, persist parent-group cancellation event, notify parent,
cancel resolved-parent siblings, propagate terminal ancestors. Each later root
loads latest shadow state, including canonical governance stripping; local held
next-record reservation is retained separately by reference for the source's
immediate postwrite calls. Missing/terminal skip behavior and per-call outbox
occurrences are preserved. Detected active-path cycles and actual conflicting
canonical/index views fail operationally with no plan. Multiple open groups or
historical backlink/partition differences are NOT corruption by inference; the
explicit compatibility disposition below governs them. Before exposure all
counter/version/outbox/ordinal/key/value checks have passed; allocate no sequence
for terminal changes and share the caller's next ordinal across suboperations.

`ActiveIndexRows` is a NEW operation-specific delta value, avoiding a change to
legacy IndexRows/IndexedBatchPlan: parallel optional due, or FIFO lane+member
with OPTIONAL head due, plus lifecycle dimensions above. The plan stores the
original accepted ActiveTimeoutView by reference-value; `record(id)` refetches
final touched or THAT original authority. No getter accepts a substitutable view.
Private `plan_fifo_heads` merges bounded changed members with each affected
complete original lane BEFORE the final trace/work admission, skips only members
actually removed/changed by this closure, and keeps an unscheduled/live head
blocking followers. It reads at most the removed original prefix plus its first
surviving member, plus bounded new touched members. Every consumed row is charged
and bound to current scoped core/order before comparisons. The trace records
only affected lane/direct-original-head reference tuples plus optional trace
owner positions (remapped to final write positions); public
`affected_fifo_heads()` derives those precomputed rows from original/final owners
without a fresh scan or budget reset. No query helper can repeatedly rescan
heads outside the admitted operation. An overlay iterator/API usable by all
existing selectors is a LATER exact consultation, not a fabricated complete
BTreeMap clone or implied parent integration from these getters.

**Pre-copy resource contract proposed for review.** TimeoutLimits is a separate
trusted immutable profile, never an entry field: positive u64 max_visits/
max_steps/max_links/max_history_deletes/max_work_bytes. Propose defaults100000
for each count and128MiB work, configurable positive without a newly invented
source hard closure ceiling. Raw roots use AdmissionLimits.batch_items; final
touched count uses that explicit configured profile, labelled NEW closure
admission rather than a source cleanup/descendant ceiling. All source cases must
select sufficient profiles. Source active/TTL<=31536000000 and total history
<=1000000 are bounded separately; hot maximum10000 is a DEFAULT, with any positive
configured maximum admitted by the source. Resolved hot also clamps to complete
history. Supplied immutable value/carry
bytes are checked by actual .len(), not claimed encoded size.

First check raw roots/counts and actual component/aggregate input bytes. Before
any reference-tree comparison, admit each lookup key's component lengths; before
any full equality or group enumeration, admit each actual consumed owner's
record/carry/group counts and bytes. Scalar trace discovery may reserve only
bounded reference/scalar containers after these checks; no owned command/token/
record/group/partition/value/history byte copy is allowed yet. Iterative stacks
have explicit positive counts, including empty groups/missing children and
duplicate visits; no zero-byte occurrence escapes the work gate. No whole-group
history scan: complete ordered history length is authority and only the required
oldest deletion prefix is consumed, bounded by max_history_deletes.

Freeze the exact trace BEFORE copied-owner admission. Let R_u be the full actual
variable bytes initially cloned ONCE for unique touched owner u (core, partition,
lineage groups/results/refs/carry/reservation). Let A_u be every new/replacement
owned byte occurrence subsequently inserted into that owner, even if an old
cloned string is freed. Let H_e be every actually copied history scalar-string/
ref/carry occurrence plus decimal event-ID length for event e. Let O_j be every
owned release intent name/ref occurrence. Let V_v be the actual independent
partition+ID byte occurrences owned by `TimeoutValueWrite` v, distinct from the
final record's Versioned ref and every parent/history ref copy. TimeoutValueWrite
owns its own ActiveValueRef plus scalar TimeoutError/expiry; charge its scalar
descriptor too. Propose
`P=sum_u(R_u+A_u)+sum_e H_e+sum_j O_j+sum_v V_v+1024*(U+E+J+V+trim_descriptors+hot_eviction_descriptors+index_descriptors+head_descriptors)`
checked against AdmissionLimits.decision_bytes before materialization. Reuse NO
ClaimPhase4x or16*A assertion: parent groups are copied once, small history fields
per event, and touched-core payload copies dominate only U, not every step.

Separately G is the sum of actual admitted full-record equality/read occurrences,
traversed group/link/key/ref/index/history-prefix bytes plus1024 for each actual
visit/group/link/step/history-row/index-row/release-row, checked against
TimeoutLimits.max_work_bytes BEFORE each represented visit/comparison. Require
P+G within the same work profile before copy. Both totals use checked u64
arithmetic and immutable logical byte/count rules, not size_of/native capacity.
Implementation must publish the actual equality/copy trace before acceptance;
an extra pass/copy requires review and corrected formula. BTree prefix comparison
and allocator/native peaks remain qualified; this is bounded represented work,
not an exact CPU/RSS guarantee. Allocation failure remains operational. Final
encoded record/value/history/outcome caps require future actual codec binding;
these logical charges cannot certify serialized bytes or reference availability.

Actually read performance's full3953–4174 trace/closure and architecture's direct

Exact proposed additional fields and shapes:

- WorkflowRecordData has id:RecordId,workflow_type/state:Vec<u8>,version:u64,
  fence:Fence,attempts:u64,created_at/updated_at:TimestampMillis,next_run_at:
  Option<TimestampMillis>,run_state:Option<Vec<u8>>,lease:Option<Lease>,payload/
  result/error:Option<Vec<u8>>,latest_kind:EventKind,latest_version:u64,
  latest_fence:Fence. The full witness must equal the admitted current version/
  fence and remain explicitly supplied; that equality is logical consistency,
  not historical provenance. The exact proposed existing WorkflowStatus change
  is ONE Unscheduled variant and fallback branch: arbitrary nonterminal state
  OTHER THAN the physical running label with next=Some is Scheduled; next=None
  is Unscheduled. Running keeps its physical-label branch, with its existing
  doc clarified to allow a restored unleased target. state/run_state/lease/
  lease_deadline getters retain actual values (absent lease=>deadline0). The
  restoration validator does not require lease/due solely from physical running.
  Existing named worker mutation guards still require actual ownership/lease
  where applicable; no reachable legacy category or duplicate predicate changes.
- ActiveValueError has exactly Domain(DomainError),Admission(AdmissionError),
  WrongPolicyType,InvalidCapturedActive,InvalidCapturedRetention,InvalidLineage,
  InvalidReservation,InvalidRefs,InvalidExtensions. It is a pure constructor/
  capture error, never evidence that a current canonical view is coherent.
  Existing Domain/Admission Display is reused; the seven new logical variants
  describe invalid captured lifecycle/type/lineage/ref/carry values and make no
  new public source error claim. The fresh reducer maps consumed-authority
  failures to InvalidAuthority, while request/profile business bounds use the
  named ActiveTimeoutRejection. TimeoutLimits::new(visits:u64,steps:u64,links:u64,
  history_deletes:u64,work_bytes:u64)->Result<Self,AdmissionError> rejects zero;
  corresponding five const getters and Default use the proposed profile above.
- ActiveCarry stores rewound_to_event_id:Option<Vec<u8>>,named_refs_history:
  Option<Vec<u8>>,attributes_history:Option<Vec<u8>>,state_meta_history:
  Option<Vec<u8>>,record_extensions:Vec<u8>. Present-empty remains present.
  Those immutable history fields are explicit actual prepared bytes; this
  constructor does not certify JSON/schema/content. Extensions preserve static
  incarnation/system/schedule/attribute/indexed-attribute data excluded from
  separately modeled fields. Timeout must neither discard them nor duplicate
  captured governance in that owner. A future canonical decoder must enforce
  that exact disjoint schema; unsupported mutation requires its own model gate.
- ActiveTimeoutView<'v> has indexed:IndexedGroupView<'v>,records:
  &'v BTreeMap<ScopedRecordId<'v>,&'v ActiveRecord>,history:
  &'v BTreeMap<ScopedRecordId<'v>,BTreeSet<HistoryKey<'v>>>,lifecycle:
  &'v BTreeMap<ActiveIndexKey<'v>,u64>,outbox:&'v ReleaseOutboxState,
  release_shard:u64. This explicit predecessor selects the due-any-ENABLED view
  profile: every applicable record has BOTH Due and DueAny authority. No boolean
  entry hint or empty-map inference controls this dimension. The indexed
  group/placement/policies and rich records have ONE canonical origin; every
  consumed core/projection must be fully equal. Complete absence/history lengths/
  lane membership are adapter obligations. Existing GroupView/IndexedGroupView
  do NOT carry tenant/recovery/RequestScope. Matching the selected release_shard,
  its complete outbox namespace and EntryOrder's applied index/ordinal to the
  SAME ordered log group AND recovery namespace is an explicit trusted outer
  apply-owner obligation,
  not type-level proof from this view or fresh-only primitive. LogIdentity itself
  also has no group/recovery fields. No new namespace
  field is proposed here; the primitive accepts no caller release destination.
  No arbitrary revision or relation-window hint proves those obligations.
- ActiveRecordWrite has expected_version:u64,record:ActiveRecord. Final touched
  order is first MUTATION occurrence, not map order; a read-only skipped root
  does not consume a write slot. expected_version ALWAYS comes from original
  authority, while record.version includes every intermediate accepted step.
- TimeoutValueWrite has reference:ActiveValueRef,body:TimeoutError,expires_at:
  Option<TimestampMillis>. Its reference is always local Versioned Error at the
  exact timeout step version. No inline encoded body or supplied length is kept.
  ReleaseIntent has flow_id:RecordId,partition:PartitionId,scope:Vec<u8>,shard_id:
  u64,reservation_id:Vec<u8>,enforcement:LimitEnforcement,created_at:TimestampMillis.
  ReleaseAppend has sequence:u64,intent:ReleaseIntent. The plan also preserves
  expected_outbox:ReleaseOutboxState and next_outbox:ReleaseOutboxState; both
  head/tail are checked before any append is exposed.
- ActiveHistory has event_id:String,event_ms:TimestampMillis,kind:EventKind,
  occurred_at:TimestampMillis,id:RecordId,partition:PartitionId,workflow_type/
  state:Vec<u8>,version:u64,priority:u8,attempts:u64,fence:Fence,created_at/
  updated_at:TimestampMillis,next_run_at:Option<TimestampMillis>,lease_deadline:
  TimestampMillis,worker:Option<Vec<u8>>,payload/result/error_ref:
  Option<ActiveValueRef>,parent_id/root_id/correlation_id/rewound_to_event_id:
  Option<Vec<u8>>,named_refs/attributes/state_meta:Option<Vec<u8>>,
  timeout:Option<TimeoutError>. This is the source scalar/ref/meta snapshot,
  not a full parent/child-group clone. It preserves nil/empty bytes separately
  before a later source projection maps selected history scalars to empty text.
  Event milliseconds use max(now,previous.updated_at), while occurred_at is now.
- HistoryKey<'v> contains event_ms:TimestampMillis,event_id:&'v[u8], ordered by
  score then actual binary ID. HistoryTrim<'v> contains owner:usize,original:
  Vec<HistoryKey<'v>>,created:Vec<usize>. Created entries are indices into owned
  history; no reference points into the same owning plan. The trim sequence
  records source after-history steps, including deletion of an event created
  earlier in this entry. Hot eviction storage is ONLY Vec<(usize,TimestampMillis,
  u64)> (owner/event-ms/version); it describes exact new terminal/prior cap1 IDs
  without another event-ID byte owner. A getter derives the scoped identity.
- ActiveIndexKey<'v> has ActiveTimeout(ScopedRecordId),TerminalRetention(
  ScopedRecordId),Due{workflow_type,state,priority:u8,record:ScopedRecordId},
  DueAny{workflow_type,priority:u8,record:ScopedRecordId},State{workflow_type,
  state,record:ScopedRecordId},Inflight{workflow_type,record:ScopedRecordId},
  Worker{worker,record:ScopedRecordId},Parent{value,record:ScopedRecordId},
  Root{value,record:ScopedRecordId},Correlation{value,record:ScopedRecordId};
  each untyped name is &'v[u8]. The map value is actual due/deadline/updated/lease
  score for that dimension. Source due/due-any rows for EVERY scheduled record,
  including FIFO followers, remain distinct from the correctness selector's
  parallel/FIFO-head representation. This dual distinction is REQUIRED by
  flow_claim_indexes.ex754–926, not a claim that existing ParallelIndex alone
  implements the source's query indexes. View validation binds both dimensions;
  this chosen enabled profile requires its row. Disabled source profiles remain
  an explicit later profile/adapter consultation, never silently counted green
  or substituted by missing rows in this predecessor.
- ActiveIndexRows<'b> is a struct with parallel:Option<DueOrder<'b>>,fifo:Option<
  (LaneKey<'b>,LaneOrder<'b>,Option<DueOrder<'b>>)>,semantic:
  [Option<(ActiveIndexKey<'b>,u64)>;10]. The two correctness fields are disjoint;
  semantic entries are a fixed maximum of TEN dimensions per record, not
  unbounded cloned durable keys or newly allocated getter spines.
  ActiveIndexDelta<'b> has before:Option<ActiveIndexRows<'b>>,after:Option<
  ActiveIndexRows<'b>>. Private ActiveIndexChange<'v> has before:&'v ActiveRecord,
  write:usize,before_mode:StateMode,after_mode:StateMode. Before semantic rows
  derive from original authority; after rows derive under the plan borrow from
  writes[write].record. No stored owner refers to itself. These fixed borrowed
  row arrays are stack values; getter formation performs no additional full
  canonical equality/lookup. Redundant same-key/same-score before/after rows are
  allowed rather than introducing a free variable-byte equality pass. Future
  transport still accounts for repeated consumption of these bounded values.
  Exact helper signatures are
  `active_rows<'b>(record:&'b ActiveRecord,mode:StateMode)

Exact private scalar/reference models in proposed trace/state.rs:

- TraceValueRef<'v> is Original(&'v ActiveValueRef) or Timeout{owner:usize,
  version:u64}; it describes a future copied ref without generating key bytes.
- ShadowRecord<'v> has original:&'v ActiveRecord,latest_step:Option<usize>,
  group_updates:Vec<usize>. A unique BTreeMap<ScopedRecordId<'v>,usize> points to
  its stable Vec position. It holds no cloned record, partition, payload or group.
- ShadowGroup<'v> has owner:usize,id:&'v[u8],original:&'v ChildGroup,prior:
  Option<usize>,summary:ChildSummary,resolved:Option<ChildResolution>,updates:
  Vec<(&'v RecordId,ChildStatus,Option<(ChildStatus,Option<TraceValueRef<'v>>,
  Option<TraceValueRef<'v>>)>)>. Cancel-result refs are absent; terminal-result
  refs preserve source originals or a prior timeout identity. Every changed child
  is one admitted scalar/reference occurrence. The prior chain and each lookup
  visit are bounded/charged; no implicit full-map clone occurs while tracing.
- TimeoutStep<'v> has owner:usize,previous:Option<usize>,group_checkpoint:usize,
  kind:EventKind,version:u64,state:&'v[u8],updated_at:TimestampMillis,next_run_at:
  Option<TimestampMillis>,lease:Option<&'v Lease>,ttl_ms:Option<u64>,retention_until:
  Option<TimestampMillis>,error_ref:Option<TraceValueRef<'v>>,timeout:
  Option<TimeoutError>,ordering:OrderingMetadata,held_reservation:
  Option<&'v GovernanceReservation>. Attempts/fence/creation/run-state and other
  unchanged source fields resolve from original. Static terminal labels also
  outlive 'v. group_checkpoint freezes that held source snapshot's group prefix;
  later original-root loads use latest_step. Stored non-running refetch strips
  reservation while an immediate frame uses held_reservation at that step.
- TimeoutFrame has EXACT variants ExpireRoot{owner:usize},CancelClosed{owner:
  usize,held_step:usize},CancelChild{owner:usize},FinishCancelledGroups{owner:
  usize,held_step:usize,patches:Vec<usize>},NotifyParent{child:usize,held_step:
  usize,status:ChildStatus},PropagateParent{owner:usize,held_step:usize},
  LeavePath{owner:usize}. Missing children are admitted skipped lookups before
  any CancelChild frame; prepared parent-group patches become visible only at
  the source's later parent write. CancelChild schedules ONLY its cancelled
  step/after-history/descendant-closure frames, NEVER NotifyParent. Expired roots
  and resolved terminal parent propagation retain their source notification
  points; this avoids double-counting the separately cancelled parent group.
  Active dependency paths detect cycles, while
  repeated roots/resolved parents are not relabelled cycles. Each frame visit
  takes prospective max_visits/+1024 work admission before processing.
- TimeoutTrace<'v> has view:ActiveTimeoutView<'v>,now:TimestampMillis,order:
  EntryOrder,owners:Vec<ShadowRecord<'v>>,lookup:BTreeMap<ScopedRecordId<'v>,usize>,
  groups:Vec<ShadowGroup<'v>>,steps:Vec<TimeoutStep<'v>>,frames:Vec<TimeoutFrame>,
  path:BTreeSet<ScopedRecordId<'v>>,trims:Vec<HistoryTrim<'v>>,hot_evictions:
  Vec<(usize,TimestampMillis,u64)>,heads:
  Vec<(LaneKey<'v>,Option<(Option<usize>,&'v ActiveRecord)>)>,
  values:Vec<(usize,u64,u64)>,releases:Vec<(usize,&'v GovernanceReservation,
  TimestampMillis)>,expected_outbox/next_outbox:ReleaseOutboxState,expired_roots:
  u64,next_ordinal:Option<u32>,consumed_ordinals:u64,charge:TimeoutCharge.
  Value tuples mean owner/version/duration; release tuples retain each qualifying
  call. All owned Vec/trees here contain ONLY scalars/original refs. Freezing this
  trace precedes one materialization pass and any variable byte clone.

phase error can coexist with earlier committed records, even though the public
return is an error. That is observably different from the Rust design's one
original request outcome and atomic same-group effects. Proposed Rust parent
selection: gate ONCE, build all phases over one scalar overlay, and persist one
all-effects outcome atomically; preserve source phase/order/quotas but explicitly
record the partial-observation migration in an ADR/conformance rule. Do NOT
reinterpret a source Router error as proof that earlier writes did not commit.
If a legacy separate-write surface is required, it needs its own versioned
outcome/failure contract; it cannot masquerade as this atomic parent.

including foreign or repeated values. The used-set cardinality is therefore
≤U≤1000; refund references≤R≤1000. This is a new bounded planning-observation
profile, not a claimed cap in source governance_release_ids itself. Invalid
used count/leaf is InvalidCreditAuthority, never a retained workflow rejection.

current aggregate work is checked again even for a previously admitted batch.
Only admit_claim_credit_batch constructs the reserved-ID duplicate set AFTER
complete G+P admission. Its private immutable Batch thereafter proves VALUE
uniqueness only: the safe borrowed ID spine/bytes cannot mutate during that
borrow. Settlement rechecks CURRENT R/U counts, scope/shard/epoch, all actual
lengths/occurrences and work but builds NO second reserved duplicate set.
It relies on that established uniqueness, never external spend/lease authority.
Accepted uses identity membership, handles repeated used occurrences and a
non-prefix subset, and returns original reservation references in original
order. Unrelated used IDs are ignored as the source set-difference helper does;
the future parent must independently bind every accepted record reservation
to its verified batch BEFORE constructing this observation. KnownNoCommit
refunds all; it means externally established ATOMIC no-commit, never any source
Router error after earlier phases. UnknownCommit and Unclassified allocate no
refund spine and release none. Unknown spend preserves its original Batch IDs
and prohibits proceeding to a claim/new spend until the authoritative owner
has resolved/inquired/explicitly compensated them. No boolean definitely_empty
can turn a failed spend into success here. The source failed-spend empty case
requires the later authoritative applicable-phase presence proof.

Proposed OPERATION-LOCAL charge before quota/refund ownership:
`Q=sum all normalized caller leaf OCCURRENCES`; `E=sum(C0+Ci)` for every full
coalesced compatibility comparison. `K_pre` sizes every actual installed type,
binary version, type/state retry target/catalogue key PLUS each projection key;
`K_validate` repeats the installed variable bytes for the existing borrowed
validate_stored_policy pass; `K_catalog` adds both actual key occurrences for
every exact sorted catalogue comparison; `K_type` adds both exact type operands;
`K_resolve` adds each actual requested key before lookup (Any instead adds each
actual catalogue key before its rule iteration). Rule merging is scalar and
does not copy/recompare the selected binary key. K is their checked sum, not a
single-pass attribution. Counts/lengths and the prospective whole pass charge
precede that pass's validation/equality/lookup; a looser earlier constructor
confers no current resource allowance. `I=sum reserved/used ID occurrences PLUS
batch scope and BOTH explicit-demand scope comparison occurrences`.
`N=sum caller state/partition/value spine occurrence counts`; S is complete
catalogue rows, M resolved base/requested-state occurrences (Any gives1+S).
`G=Q+E+K+I+1024*C+64*(N+4*S+M+R+U)`; 4*S represents2*S initial stored/projection
row sizing, S immutable validation and S exact catalogue comparison. C/N/Q/E
are pre-admitted before ANY caller leaf comparison. For the implicit resolver,
that same operation then admits all projection passes before resolution.
The constructor's catalogue admission and a later resolver's re-admission are
SEPARATE public operations, each fully charged; neither inherits a consumed
shared budget or claims a cross-call total bound. No-rule implicit still pays
catalogue validation; explicit bypass has K/S/M=0 and touches no unused policy.
Credit operations use C/N/E/K/S/M=0 and charge every R/U count before leaf reads.
P is a selected OPERATION-LOCAL LOGICAL descriptor estimate, not size_of/native
layout: schedule64*C; batch duplicate admission64*R; Accepted settlement16*R+
64*U; KnownNoCommit settlement16*R; UnknownCommit/Unclassified settlement0.
P uses ALL reserved/used occurrences BEFORE set construction,
not distinct/refund counts learned afterwards. Peak settlement owners are ONE
temporary used set≤U plus ONE refund spine≤R; batch admission instead has ONE
duplicate set≤R with no refund spine. KnownNoCommit has refund spine≤R/no set;
UnknownCommit/Unclassified retain no refund spine/set (P=0 for that branch).
All G+P gates precede quota Vec, set or output-spine ownership. Non-applicable
terms are zero, not artificial unused authority traversal.
Repeated getter/tree-prefix comparisons and host allocation are
not thereby a CPU/RSS bound. The temporary set and output spine can coexist;
BTree allocation remains ordinary host-failure behavior. Required source
profiles must choose sufficient immutable limits; arbitrary caller values cannot
raise them. ARCH/PERF must settle exact visit/occurrence and peak-spine counts
against the actual proposed helpers before implementation, including the
optional-policy/explicit branch and all deferred observation paths.
phase/advance/allocations can perform additional bounded scalar C visits;
repeating a public invocation/getter does not consume a shared global counter.
Initial G is not a certificate for arbitrarily many later reads. The required
parent must prospectively charge its actual scalar iterations/comparisons
under ONE shared accumulator before using these schedules in a private atomic
composition; that parent API/trace remains a separate named consultation.

#### Pre-copy work, source byte semantics and authority

S=complete states, H=present state-governance groups (H<=S), R=all actual limit/budget/circuit
rows, L=all normalized string-list OCCURRENCES, I=indexed-name occurrences.
Before traversal/comparison/set allocation: admit S, each rule-map count<=1000,
each list count<=1000 and normalized metadata counts3/1. Charge positive row work
even for empty groups/zero-byte malformed names. K includes EVERY actual binary
occurrence: type/version/retry targets/state names; rule names/unit/list/
error-class names; indexed names. Each state key has ONE owner; present outer
Option groups pay their own scalar descriptor visits without a second key.
Length-check all operands before state-name equality, duplicate membership or
name lookup.
Do not scan or compare an enormous requested name merely to discover its charge.
The two metrics helpers take the SAME mutable charge so their discovery passes
cannot first enumerate the entire maximum-state/rule/list product and only then
reject an over-budget aggregate. Check an enclosing container's len BEFORE its
entries, charge128 for each prospective descriptor BEFORE entering it, and check
a leaf's actual len before admitting its byte occurrence. All count discovery
and later byte/validation passes pay their own occurrences. The whole no-owner
preflight finishes before any canonical-list set. This bounds permitted logical
work incrementally; it does not pretend that nested counts are readable without
their actual descriptor visits.

Proposal literal logical estimate per actual sizing/validation pass:
G += K_pass +128*N_pass; N_pass includes each actual core/state/governance/rule/
list/index descriptor inspected, including empty groups.
N's exact descriptor grammar is: one complete-data root, one states container,
one descriptor per state entry; one for each PRESENT retry/backoff/retention,
governance/effects/audit/approvals or rule-map container; one per rule entry;
one per PRESENT string-list container and each of its entries; one per PRESENT
indexed-attributes container/entry and indexed-state-meta value. Each descriptor
covers its fixed typed scalar slots; absence is read as a fixed slot and creates
no extra optional descriptor. Rule unit/version/target/name leaf bytes are in K,
with their fixed Option slot covered by the enclosing descriptor. Discovery,
byte sizing, scalar validation and canonical membership use only the descriptors
they ACTUALLY revisit, plus the explicitly conservative full core-pass estimate.
No parent budget may count a completed sizing traversal as a free validator.
The reused core-field validators and later current-profile re-admission are
additional passes, not free use of
the first K. Before calling validate_complete_core, reserve a
further complete K+128*N pass from the already admitted metrics; using the
complete-schema estimate for that narrower core pass is conservative and
explicit. Field validators similarly admit their actual prospective occurrence
before any variable comparison. Selecting state governance charges the actual
requested state length+128 BEFORE the single complete-state lookup; absent or
unknown state falls back to type/default content as source resolve does.

Some(8),\n                half_open_success_threshold: Some(9),\n                error_classes: Some(vec![b\"timeout\".to_vec()]),\n            },\n        )])),\n        approvals: Some(ApprovalsData {\n            effects: Some(vec![b\"pay\".to_vec()]),\n            states: Some(vec![b\"ready\".to_vec()]),\n            assignees: Some(vec![b\"ops\".to_vec()]),\n            timeout_ms: Some(11),\n for generation in [0, MAX_POLICY_GENERATION + 1] {\n        let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(profile);\n        assert_eq!(\n            restore_complete_policy(\n                generation,\n Some(PolicySchemaError::Policy(PolicyError::InvalidGeneration))\n        );\n        assert_eq!(charge.total(), 0);\n    }\n    for version in [Some(PolicyVersion::Bytes(Vec::new()))] {\n        let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(profile);\n        assert_eq!(\n            restore_complete_policy(\n                1,\n                data(vec![b'r'], version, BTreeMap::new()),\n                profile,\n                &mut charge\n            )\n            .err(),\n            Some(PolicySchemaError::Policy(PolicyError::InvalidVersion))\n        );\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn Some(3),\n                }),\n                governance: Some(GovernanceData {\n                    mode: Some(GovernanceMode::Ledger),\n                    effects: None,\n                    audit: None,\n                    limits: Some(BTreeMap::from([(\n                        b\"running\".to_vec(),\n                        LimitData {\n                            limit: 0,\n circuits: None,\n                    approvals: None,\n                }),\n            },\n        ),\n        (\n            b\"other\".to_vec(),\n            CompleteStatePolicyData {\n states), profile, &mut charge)?;\n    assert_complete_state(&restored, state_owner, target_owner)?;\n    for name in [Vec::new(), b\"running\".to_vec()] {\n        let states = BTreeMap::from([(\n            name,\n            CompleteStatePolicyData {\n                mode: None,\n                retry: None,\n                retention: None,\n                governance: None,\n            },\n profile = limits(128 * 1_024 * 1_024)?;\n    for (range, length, error) in [\n        (0..262_144, 262_144, None),\n        (1..262_145, 263_168, None),\n        (0..262_145, 262_145, candidate(\n            1,\n            data(vec![b'r'], None, BTreeMap::new()),\n            profile,\n            &mut charge,\n        )?;\n        let encoded = vec![0x33; length];\n        let owner = encoded.as_ptr();\n        let result = prepared.bind_encoded_snapshot(range, encoded, profile, &mut charge);\n        if let Some(error) = error {\n            assert_eq!(result.err(), One immutable profile and a continuous logical occurrence/scratch account.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\nuse crate::policy::installation::{PolicyError, PolicyLimits};\nuse crate::workflow::admission::AdmissionError;\n\nuse super::{\n    CompletePolicyData, GovernanceData, GovernanceField, GovernanceRuleKind, PolicySchemaError,\n};\n\n/// Immutable normalized-content and represented-work admission profile.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]\npub struct PolicySchemaLimits {\n    states: PolicyLimits,\n    work_bytes: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Default for PolicySchemaLimits {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            states: PolicyLimits::default(),\n            work_bytes: 128 * 1_024 * 1_024,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl PolicySchemaLimits {\n    /// Selects a nonzero work profile without granting caller authority to raise it.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    /// Returns `InvalidLimits` for a zero represented-work maximum.\n    pub fn new(states: PolicyLimits, work_bytes: u64) -> Result<Self, AdmissionError> {\n        if work_bytes == 0 {\n            return Err(AdmissionError::InvalidLimits);\n        }\n        Ok(Self { states, work_bytes })\n    }\n\n    /// Reads the selected existing core state profile.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn policy_limits(self) -> PolicyLimits {\n        self.states\n    }\n\n    /// Reads the immutable represented-work maximum.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn max_work_bytes(self) -> u64 {\n        self.work_bytes\n    }\n}\n\n/// Continuous logical work and peak scratch for one parent-owned account.\n///\n/// Matching profiles do not prove accounting identity. The authoritative parent\n/// must thread the same account through all operations; there is no reset/debit API.\n/// Input construction, refused-owner destruction and native capacity/CPU/RSS are\n/// outside this represented estimate and require bounded outer preparation.\npub struct PolicySchemaCharge {\n    limits: PolicySchemaLimits,\n    g: u64,\n    p: u64,\n}\n\nimpl PolicySchemaCharge {\n    /// Begins one empty account under the immutable supplied profile.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn new(limits: PolicySchemaLimits) -> Self {\n        Self { limits, g: 0, p: 0 }\n    }\n\n    /// Reads admitted cumulative occurrence work.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn g(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.g\n    }\n\n    /// Reads admitted peak logical scratch, retained after temporary sets
