        assert_eq!(original_hash.as_slice(), &expected[29..61]);
        assert_eq!(case == 5, original_hash != super::MINIMAL_INTENT_DIGEST);
    }
    for guard in [None, Some(0), Some(u64::MAX)] {
        let mut intent = MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES.to_vec();
        if let Some(value) = guard {
            let mut payload = vec![1];
            payload.extend_from_slice(&value.to_be_bytes());
            drop(intent.splice(35..36, payload));
        }
        let stamp = CommittedTime::new(HlcTimestamp::new(0, 0)?, 0)?;
        let expected = replace_frame_literal(&intent, [b"t", b"g", b"r", b"q"], stamp)?;
        let (caller, bytes, frame) = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame_caller(
            super::input(minimal_data(), guard)?,
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            &mut charge,
        )?;
        assert_eq!(caller.input().expected_generation(), guard);
        assert!(caller.input().data() == &minimal_data());
        assert!(caller.schema_limits() == limits);
        assert_eq!(caller.admission_limits(), AdmissionLimits::default());
        assert_eq!((bytes, frame), (intent.len(), expected.len()));
        let prepared = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            super::input(minimal_data(), guard)?,
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            &mut charge,
        )?;
        assert_eq!(prepared.as_bytes(), expected);
        assert_eq!(
            prepared.digest(),
            PreparedDigest::new(Sha256::digest(&expected).into())
        );
        assert_eq!(&prepared.as_bytes()[83..], intent);
    }
    assert_eq!(
        ClientIntent::new(2, [0; 32]),
        Err(RequestValueError::UnsupportedVersion)
    );
    Ok(())
}

fn complete_replace_frame_enforces_whole_scope_raw_count_and_list_canonicality_priority()

    let wrong = profile(1_000_000_001)?;
    let before = (charge.g(), charge.p());

        CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(
            PolicySchemaError::ProfileMismatch
        ))
    );
    let result = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
        &expected,
        wrong,
        AdmissionLimits::default(),
        &mut charge,
    );

        result.err().ok_or("profile verifier refusal")?,
        CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(
            PolicySchemaError::ProfileMismatch
        ))
    );
    assert_eq!((charge.g(), charge.p()), before);
    for maximum in [134, 135] {

            );
            assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 1_543);

}

        let expected = replace_frame_hex(FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES[0].0)?;
        let result = if producer {

                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                &mut charge,
            )
            .map(|_| ())
        } else {
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                &expected,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                &mut charge,
            )
            .map(|_| ())
        };
        assert_eq!(
            result,
            Err(CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(
                CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(PolicySchemaError::WorkBytes {
                    bytes: target,
                    maximum
                })
            ))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            (charge.g(), charge.p(), charge.total()),
            (retained, 0, retained)
        );
    }
    let limits = profile(1_543)?;
    let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(limits);
    let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
        super::input(minimal_data(), None)?,
        limits,
        AdmissionLimits::new(1_048_576, 134, 1_000)?,
        &mut charge,
    );
    assert_eq!(
        result.err().ok_or("F cap before Q")?,
        CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::ByteLimit)
    );
    assert_eq!((charge.g(), charge.p()), (1_543, 0));
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn replace_frame_hex(hex: &str) -> TestResult<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    for pair in hex.as_bytes().as_chunks::<2>().0 {
        bytes.push(u8::from_str_radix(std::str::from_utf8(pair)?, 16)?);
    }
    assert_eq!(bytes.len() * 2, hex.len());
    Ok(bytes)
}

pub(super) fn replace_frame_input(
    data: CompletePolicyData,
    guard: Option<u64>,
    ids: [&[u8]; 4],
    stamp: CommittedTime,
) -> TestResult<CompletePolicyReplaceInput> {
    Ok(CompletePolicyReplaceInput::new(
        RequestScope::new(
            TenantId::new(ids[0].to_vec())?,
            GroupId::new(ids[1].to_vec())?,
            RecoveryId::new(ids[2].to_vec())?,
        ),
        RequestId::new(ids[3].to_vec())?,
        stamp,
        guard,
        data,
    ))
}

pub(super) fn replace_frame_literal(
    intent: &[u8],
    ids: [&[u8]; 4],
    stamp: CommittedTime,
) -> TestResult<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut expected = b"FWCP\0\x01\x06".to_vec();
    for id in ids {
        expected.extend_from_slice(&u32::try_from(id.len())?.to_be_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(id);
    }
    expected.extend_from_slice(b"\0\x02");
    expected.extend_from_slice(&<[u8; 32]>::from(Sha256::digest(intent)));
    expected.extend_from_slice(&stamp.hlc().physical().get().to_be_bytes());
    expected.extend_from_slice(&stamp.hlc().logical().to_be_bytes());
    expected.extend_from_slice(&stamp.wall().get().to_be_bytes());
    expected.extend_from_slice(&u32::try_from(intent.len())?.to_be_bytes());
    expected.extend_from_slice(intent);
    Ok(expected)
}

pub(super) fn assert_replace_frame_verified(
    verified: &VerifiedCompletePolicyReplaceFrame<'_>,
    expected: &[u8],
    log: LogIdentity,
) {
    let mut cursor = 7;
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    let mut scope = b"FWSC\0\x01".to_vec();
    for index in 0..4 {
        assert_eq!(&expected[cursor..cursor + 2], &[0, 0]);
        let length = usize::from(u16::from_be_bytes(
            expected[cursor + 2..cursor + 4].as_chunks::<2>().0[0],
        ));
        if index < 3 {
            scope.extend_from_slice(&expected[cursor..cursor + 4]);
        }
        cursor += 4;
        ids.push(&expected[cursor..cursor + length]);
        if index < 3 {
            scope.extend_from_slice(ids[index]);
        }
        cursor += length;
    }
    let original = &expected[cursor + 56..];
    let digest = PreparedDigest::new(Sha256::digest(expected).into());
    let intent: [u8; 32] = Sha256::digest(original).into();
    let physical = u64::from_be_bytes(expected[cursor + 34..cursor + 42].as_chunks::<8>().0[0]);
    let logical = u16::from_be_bytes(expected[cursor + 42..cursor + 44].as_chunks::<2>().0[0]);
    let wall = u64::from_be_bytes(expected[cursor + 44..cursor + 52].as_chunks::<8>().0[0]);
    let header = verified.header(log);
    assert_eq!(verified.encoded(), expected);
    assert_eq!(verified.original_intent(), original);
    assert_eq!(verified.digest(), digest);
    assert_eq!(verified.isolation_scope(), scope);
    assert_eq!(header.format_version, 1);
    assert_eq!(header.scope.tenant().as_bytes(), ids[0]);
    assert_eq!(header.scope.group().as_bytes(), ids[1]);
    assert_eq!(header.scope.recovery().as_bytes(), ids[2]);
    assert_eq!(header.request.as_bytes(), ids[3]);
    assert_eq!(header.intent.version(), 2);
    assert_eq!(*header.intent.digest(), intent);
    assert_eq!(header.stamp.hlc().physical().get(), physical);
    assert_eq!(header.stamp.hlc().logical(), logical);
    assert_eq!(header.stamp.wall().get(), wall);
    assert_eq!(header.identity, EntryIdentity::new(log, digest));
    assert_eq!(header.encoded_entry, expected);
    assert_eq!(header.encoded_isolation_scope, scope);
}

pub(super) fn assert_replace_frame_account(
    maximum: u64,
    producer: bool,
    repeated: bool,
    held_peak: bool,
) -> TestResult {
    let limits = profile(maximum)?;
    let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(limits);
    let mut seed_data = minimal_data();
    seed_data.indexed_attributes = Some(vec![b"a".to_vec()]);
    let seed = if held_peak {
        Some(restore_complete_policy(1, seed_data, limits, &mut charge)?)
    } else {
        None
    };
    let expected = replace_frame_hex(FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES[0].0)?;
    let mut produced = Vec::new();
    let mut verified = Vec::new();
    let fee = if producer { 4_612 } else { 4_423 };
    let attempts = if repeated { 2 } else { 1 };
    let initial = if held_peak { 1_928 } else { 0 };
    let peak = if held_peak { 64 } else { 0 };
    assert_eq!((charge.g(), charge.p()), (initial, peak));
    for attempt in 1..=attempts {
        let target = initial + fee * attempt + peak;
        let result = if producer {
            prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                super::super::input(minimal_data(), None)?,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                &mut charge,
            )
            .map(|value| produced.push(value))
        } else {
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                &expected,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                &mut charge,
            )
            .map(|value| verified.push(value))
        };
        if maximum < target {
            assert_eq!(
                result,
                Err(CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(
                    CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(PolicySchemaError::WorkBytes {
                        bytes: target,
                        maximum
                    })
                ))
            );
            assert_eq!(
                (charge.g(), charge.p(), charge.total()),
                (target - peak - 263, peak, target - 263)
            );
        } else {
            result?;
            assert_eq!(
                (charge.g(), charge.p(), charge.total()),
                (target - peak, peak, target)
            );
        }
    }
    for value in &produced {
        assert_eq!(value.as_bytes(), expected);
        assert_eq!(
            value.digest(),
            PreparedDigest::new(Sha256::digest(&expected).into())
        );
    }
    for value in &verified {
        assert_replace_frame_verified(
            value,
            &expected,
            LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
        );
    }
    if let Some(seed) = seed {
        let mut expected = minimal_data();
        expected.indexed_attributes = Some(vec![b"a".to_vec()]);
        assert!(seed.data() == &expected);
        assert_eq!(seed.generation(), 1);
    }
    assert_eq!(charge.p(), peak);
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn assert_replace_frame_boundary(
    case: usize,
    limits: PolicySchemaLimits,
    charge: &mut PolicySchemaCharge,
) -> TestResult {
    let stamp = CommittedTime::new(HlcTimestamp::new(0, 0)?, 0)?;
    if case == 0 {
        for length in [8_172, 8_173] {
            let tenant = vec![b't'; length];
            let mut intent = MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES.to_vec();
            let mut raw = u32::try_from(length)?.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
            raw.extend_from_slice(&tenant);
            drop(intent.splice(30..35, raw));
            let ids = [&tenant[..], b"g", b"r", b"q"];
            let expected = replace_frame_literal(&intent, ids, stamp)?;
            let before = charge.g();
            let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                replace_frame_input(minimal_data(), None, ids, stamp)?,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge,
            );
            if length == 8_173 {
                assert_eq!(
                    result.err().ok_or("scope +1 producer")?,
                    CompletePolicyRequestError::ScopeLimit
                );
                assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 128);
                let before = charge.g();
                assert_eq!(
                    verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                        &expected,
                        limits,
                        AdmissionLimits::default(),
                        charge
                    )
                    .err()
                    .ok_or("scope +1 verifier")?,
                    CompletePolicyRequestError::ScopeLimit
                );
                assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 8_706);
            } else {
                let prepared = result?;
                assert_eq!(prepared.as_bytes(), expected);
                assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 86_322);
                let before = charge.g();
                let verified = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                    prepared.as_bytes(),
                    limits,
                    AdmissionLimits::default(),
                    charge,
                )?;
                assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 94_304);
                assert_replace_frame_verified(
                    &verified,
                    &expected,
                    LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
                );
            }
        }
    } else if case == 1 {
        for count in [
            limits.policy_limits().max_states(),
            limits.policy_limits().max_states() + 1,
        ] {
            let mut data = minimal_data();
            let mut intent = MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES.to_vec();
            intent[45..49].copy_from_slice(&u32::try_from(count)?.to_be_bytes());
            let mut entries = Vec::new();
            for name in 0..count {
                let key = u16::try_from(name)?.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
                data.states.insert(
                    key.clone(),
                    CompleteStatePolicyData {
                        mode: None,
                        retry: None,
                        retention: None,
                        governance: None,
                    },
                );
                entries.extend_from_slice(b"\0\0\0\x02");
                entries.extend_from_slice(&key);
                entries.extend_from_slice(&[0; 4]);
            }
            drop(intent.splice(49..49, entries));
            let expected = replace_frame_literal(&intent, [b"t", b"g", b"r", b"q"], stamp)?;
            let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                super::super::input(data, None)?,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge,
            );
            if count > limits.policy_limits().max_states() {
                assert_eq!(
                    result.err().ok_or("state count +1")?,
                    CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::ItemLimit)
                );
            } else {
                let prepared = result?;
                assert_eq!(prepared.as_bytes(), expected);
                let verified = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                    prepared.as_bytes(),
                    limits,
                    AdmissionLimits::default(),
                    charge,
                )?;
                assert_replace_frame_verified(
                    &verified,
                    &expected,
                    LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
                );
            }
        }
    } else if case == 2 {
        for count in [3, 4] {
            let mut data = minimal_data();
            let mut wire = vec![1];
            wire.extend_from_slice(&u32::try_from(count)?.to_be_bytes());
            let mut names = Vec::new();
            for name in 0..count {
                let key = u8::try_from(name)?.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
                wire.extend_from_slice(b"\0\0\0\x01");
                wire.extend_from_slice(&key);
                names.push(key);
            }
            data.indexed_attributes = Some(names);
            let mut intent = MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES.to_vec();
            drop(intent.splice(49..50, wire));
            let expected = replace_frame_literal(&intent, [b"t", b"g", b"r", b"q"], stamp)?;
            let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                super::super::input(data, None)?,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge,
            );
            if count == 4 {
                assert_eq!(
                    result.err().ok_or("indexed count +1")?,
                    CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::ItemLimit)
                );
            } else {
                let prepared = result?;
                assert_eq!(prepared.as_bytes(), expected);
                let verified = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                    prepared.as_bytes(),
                    limits,
                    AdmissionLimits::default(),
                    charge,
                )?;
                assert_replace_frame_verified(
                    &verified,
                    &expected,
                    LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
                );
            }
        }
    } else if case == 3 {
        for length in [262_060, 262_061] {
            let mut data = minimal_data();
            let mut intent = MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES.to_vec();
            intent[45..49].copy_from_slice(&4_u32.to_be_bytes());
            let mut entries = Vec::new();
            for first in 0..4 {
                let count = if first == 3 { length } else { 262_144 };
                let mut key = vec![0; count];
                key[0] = first;
                entries.extend_from_slice(&u32::try_from(count)?.to_be_bytes());
                entries.extend_from_slice(&key);
                entries.extend_from_slice(&[0; 4]);
                data.states.insert(
                    key,
                    CompleteStatePolicyData {
                        mode: None,
                        retry: None,
                        retention: None,
                        governance: None,
                    },
                );
            }
            drop(intent.splice(49..49, entries));
            let expected = replace_frame_literal(&intent, [b"t", b"g", b"r", b"q"], stamp)?;
            let before = charge.g();
            let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                super::super::input(data, None)?,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge,
            );
            if length == 262_061 {
                assert_eq!(
                    result.err().ok_or("whole intent +1")?,
                    CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::ByteLimit)
                );
                assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 1_050_240);
            } else {
                let prepared = result?;
                assert_eq!(intent.len(), 1_048_576);
                assert_eq!(prepared.as_bytes(), expected);
                assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 6_299_340);
                let verified = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                    prepared.as_bytes(),
                    limits,
                    AdmissionLimits::default(),
                    charge,
                )?;
                assert_replace_frame_verified(
                    &verified,
                    &expected,
                    LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
                );
            }
        }
    } else if case == 4 {
        let minimum = replace_frame_hex(FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES[0].0)?;
        for end in 0..minimum.len() {
            assert!(
                verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                    &minimum[..end],
                    limits,
                    AdmissionLimits::default(),
                    charge
                )
                .is_err()
            );
        }
        for (offset, value, error) in [
            (0, b'X', CompletePolicyEncodingError::Malformed),
            (5, 2, CompletePolicyEncodingError::UnsupportedVersion),
            (6, 5, CompletePolicyEncodingError::UnsupportedTag),
            (28, 1, CompletePolicyEncodingError::UnsupportedVersion),
            (83, b'X', CompletePolicyEncodingError::Malformed),
            (118, 2, CompletePolicyEncodingError::InvalidOptionality),
            (124, 2, CompletePolicyEncodingError::InvalidOptionality),
        ] {
            let mut bytes = minimum.clone();
            bytes[offset] = value;
            assert_eq!(
                verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                    &bytes,
                    limits,
                    AdmissionLimits::default(),
                    charge
                )
                .err()
                .ok_or("malformed mutation")?,
                CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(error)
            );
        }
        let mut bytes = minimum.clone();
        bytes.push(0);
        assert_eq!(
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                &bytes,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge
            )
            .err()
            .ok_or("trailing frame")?,
            CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::TrailingBytes)
        );
        let mut bytes = minimum.clone();
        bytes[34 + 83] = b'u';
        assert_eq!(
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                &bytes,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge
            )
            .err()
            .ok_or("tenant mismatch")?,
            CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::Malformed)
        );
        let mut bytes = minimum.clone();
        bytes[29] ^= 1;
        assert_eq!(
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                &bytes,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge
            )
            .err()
            .ok_or("digest mismatch")?,
            CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::EncodingMismatch)
        );
        let mut full = replace_frame_hex(FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES[1].0)?;
        for (offset, value) in [
            (42, 2),
            (65, 4),
            (114, 2),
            (165, 3),
            (188, 2),
            (193, 3),
            (213, 2),
        ] {
            let previous = full[83 + offset];
            full[83 + offset] = value;
            assert!(
                verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                    &full,
                    limits,
                    AdmissionLimits::default(),
                    charge
                )
                .is_err()
            );
            full[83 + offset] = previous;
        }
    } else {
        return Err("unknown independent boundary case".into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

    let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(limits);
    for (case, (hex, hash)) in FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES.iter().enumerate() {
        let expected = replace_frame_hex(hex)?;
        let digest: [u8; 32] = replace_frame_hex(hash)?
            .try_into()
            .map_err(|_| "fixed digest width")?;
        let original = if case == 0 {
            MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES
        } else {
            PRESENT_INTENT_BYTES
        };
        let data = if case == 0 {
            minimal_data()
        } else {
            present_data()
        };
        assert_eq!(&expected[83..], original);
        assert_eq!(<[u8; 32]>::from(Sha256::digest(&expected)), digest);
        let input = super::input(data, None)?;
        let before = charge.g();
        let prepared = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            input,
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            &mut charge,
        )?;
        assert_eq!(prepared.as_bytes(), expected);
        assert_eq!(prepared.digest(), PreparedDigest::new(digest));
        let (producer, verifier, peak) = if case == 0 {
            (4_612, 4_423, 0)
        } else {
            (47_249, 22_427, 128)
        };
        assert_eq!((charge.g(), charge.p()), (before + producer, peak));
        let verified = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            prepared.as_bytes(),
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            &mut charge,
        )?;
        assert_eq!(
            (charge.g(), charge.p()),
            (before + producer + verifier, peak)
        );
        assert_replace_frame_verified(
            &verified,
            &expected,
            LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
        );
        assert_eq!(verified.encoded().as_ptr(), prepared.as_bytes().as_ptr());
        assert_eq!(
            verified.original_intent().as_ptr(),
            prepared.as_bytes()[83..].as_ptr()
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn complete_replace_frame_binds_header_operands_without_binding_assigned_generation() -> TestResult
{
    let limits = profile(100_000_000)?;
    let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(limits);
    let first = prepare_complete_policy_value_v2(
        restore_complete_policy(1, minimal_data(), limits, &mut charge)?,
        limits,
        &mut charge,
    )?;
    let later = prepare_complete_policy_value_v2(
        restore_complete_policy(9, minimal_data(), limits, &mut charge)?,
        limits,
        &mut charge,
    )?;
    let mut expected_value = replace_frame_hex(
        "46575056000200000000000000010000001646575053000200000001720000000000000000000000",
    )?;
    assert_eq!(first.encoded(), expected_value);
    expected_value[6..14].copy_from_slice(&9_u64.to_be_bytes());
    assert_eq!(later.encoded(), expected_value);
    assert!(first.data() == later.data());
    assert_eq!((first.generation(), later.generation()), (1, 9));
    for (case, ids) in [*b"tgrq", *b"tGrq", *b"tgRq", *b"tgrQ", *b"tgrq", *b"ugrq"]
        .into_iter()
        .enumerate()
    {
        let stamp = if case == 4 {
            CommittedTime::new(HlcTimestamp::new(99, 7)?, 98)?
        } else {
            CommittedTime::new(HlcTimestamp::new(0, 0)?, 0)?
        };
        let ids = [&ids[0..1], &ids[1..2], &ids[2..3], &ids[3..4]];
        let mut intent = MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES.to_vec();
        intent[34] = ids[0][0];
        let expected = replace_frame_literal(&intent, ids, stamp)?;
        let prepared = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            replace_frame_input(minimal_data(), None, ids, stamp)?,
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            &mut charge,
        )?;
        assert_eq!(prepared.as_bytes(), expected);
        let verified = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            prepared.as_bytes(),
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            &mut charge,
        )?;
        for log in [
            LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
            LogIdentity::new(9, 8, AppliedPosition::new(7)),
        ] {
            assert_replace_frame_verified(&verified, &expected, log);
        }
        let original_hash: [u8; 32] = Sha256::digest(&intent).into();
        assert_eq!(original_hash.as_slice(), &expected[29..61]);
        assert_eq!(case == 5, original_hash != super::MINIMAL_INTENT_DIGEST);
    }
    for guard in [None, Some(0), Some(u64::MAX)] {
        let mut intent = MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES.to_vec();
        if let Some(value) = guard {
            let mut payload = vec![1];
            payload.extend_from_slice(&value.to_be_bytes());
            drop(intent.splice(35..36, payload));
        }
        let stamp = CommittedTime::new(HlcTimestamp::new(0, 0)?, 0)?;
        let expected = replace_frame_literal(&intent, [b"t", b"g", b"r", b"q"], stamp)?;
        let (caller, bytes, frame) = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame_caller(
            super::input(minimal_data(), guard)?,
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            &mut charge,
        )?;
        assert_eq!(caller.input().expected_generation(), guard);
        assert!(caller.input().data() == &minimal_data());
        assert!(caller.schema_limits() == limits);
        assert_eq!(caller.admission_limits(), AdmissionLimits::default());
        assert_eq!((bytes, frame), (intent.len(), expected.len()));
        let prepared = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            super::input(minimal_data(), guard)?,
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            &mut charge,
        )?;
        assert_eq!(prepared.as_bytes(), expected);
        assert_eq!(
            prepared.digest(),
            PreparedDigest::new(Sha256::digest(&expected).into())
        );
        assert_eq!(&prepared.as_bytes()[83..], intent);
    }
    assert_eq!(
        ClientIntent::new(2, [0; 32]),
        Err(RequestValueError::UnsupportedVersion)
    );
    Ok(())
}

        (89, 104, &[1, 0, 0][..]),
        (163, 394, &[1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0][..]),
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .enumerate()
    {
        let mut held = Vec::new();
        for present in [false, true] {
            let mut intent = PRESENT_INTENT_BYTES.to_vec();
            let payload = if present { empty } else { &[0][..] };
            drop(intent.splice(start..end, payload.iter().copied()));
            let expected = replace_frame_literal(&intent, [b"t", b"g", b"r", b"q"], stamp)?;
            let mut data = present_data();
            replace_frame_empty_field(&mut data, case, present)?;

            held.push(prepared);

#[test]
fn complete_replace_frame_enforces_whole_scope_raw_count_and_list_canonicality_priority()
-> TestResult {
    let limits = PolicySchemaLimits::new(PolicyLimits::new(4)?, 1_000_000_000)?;
    let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(limits);
    let expected = replace_frame_hex(FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES[0].0)?;
    let wrong = profile(1_000_000_001)?;
    let before = (charge.g(), charge.p());
    let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
        super::input(minimal_data(), None)?,
        wrong,
        AdmissionLimits::default(),
        &mut charge,
    );
    assert_eq!(
        result.err().ok_or("profile producer refusal")?,
        CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(
            PolicySchemaError::ProfileMismatch
        ))
    );
    let result = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
        &expected,
        wrong,
        AdmissionLimits::default(),
        &mut charge,
    );
    assert_eq!(
        result.err().ok_or("profile verifier refusal")?,
        CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(
            PolicySchemaError::ProfileMismatch
        ))
    );
    assert_eq!((charge.g(), charge.p()), before);
    for maximum in [134, 135] {
        let admission = AdmissionLimits::new(1_048_576, maximum, 1_000)?;
        let before = charge.g();
        let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            super::input(minimal_data(), None)?,
            limits,
            admission,
            &mut charge,
        );
        if maximum == 134 {
            assert_eq!(
                result.err().ok_or("producer F cap")?,
                CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::ByteLimit)
            );
            assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 1_543);
        } else {
            assert_eq!(result?.as_bytes(), expected);
            assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 4_612);
        }
        let before = charge.g();
        let result =
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(&expected, limits, admission, &mut charge);
        if maximum == 134 {
            assert_eq!(
                result.err().ok_or("verifier F cap")?,
                CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::ByteLimit)
            );
            assert_eq!(charge.g(), before);
        } else {
            assert_eq!(charge.g(), before + 4_423);
            assert_replace_frame_verified(
                &result?,
                &expected,
                LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
            );
        }
    }
    for case in 0..5 {
        assert_replace_frame_boundary(case, limits, &mut charge)?;
    }
    assert_replace_frame_canonical_lists(limits, &mut charge)?;
    assert_replace_frame_raw_limits(limits, &mut charge)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn complete_replace_frame_retains_each_same_account_phase_and_prior_scratch() -> TestResult {
    for producer in [false, true] {

        for (maximum, repeated, held_peak) in [

        }

        (true, 1_671, 1_543),
        (true, 2_363, 1_671),
        (true, 2_543, 2_363),
        (true, 2_806, 2_543),
        (true, 3_657, 2_806),
        (true, 4_349, 3_657),
        (true, 4_612, 4_349),
        (false, 1_673, 1_543),
        (false, 1_853, 1_673),
        (false, 2_045, 1_853),
        (false, 2_173, 2_045),
        (false, 2_301, 2_173),
        (false, 2_430, 2_301),
        (false, 2_559, 2_430),
        (false, 2_688, 2_559),
        (false, 2_817, 2_688),
        (false, 2_945, 2_817),
        (false, 3_478, 2_945),
        (false, 3_627, 3_478),
        (false, 4_160, 3_627),
        (false, 4_423, 4_160),
    ] {
        let maximum = target - 1;
        let limits = profile(maximum)?;
        let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(limits);
        let expected = replace_frame_hex(FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES[0].0)?;
        let result = if producer {
            prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                super::input(minimal_data(), None)?,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                &mut charge,
            )
            .map(|_| ())
        } else {
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                &expected,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                &mut charge,
            )
            .map(|_| ())
        };
        assert_eq!(
            result,
            Err(CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(
                CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(PolicySchemaError::WorkBytes {
                    bytes: target,
                    maximum
                })
            ))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            (charge.g(), charge.p(), charge.total()),

        );
    }
    let limits = profile(1_543)?;

    let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
        super::input(minimal_data(), None)?,
        limits,
        AdmissionLimits::new(1_048_576, 134, 1_000)?,
        &mut charge,
    );
    assert_eq!(
        result.err().ok_or("F cap before Q")?,
        CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::ByteLimit)
    );
    assert_eq!((charge.g(), charge.p()), (1_543, 0));
    Ok(())
}

//! Typed fixture edits and per-list canonicality controls.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use wf_domain::policy::RetryOverride;
use wf_domain::policy::complete::{
    ApprovalsData, AuditData, CompletePolicyData, CompletePolicyEncodingError,
    CompletePolicyReplaceInput, CompletePolicyRequestError, DenialAuditMode, EffectsData,
    GovernanceData, GovernanceMode, PolicySchemaCharge, PolicySchemaError, PolicySchemaLimits,
};
use wf_domain::policy::definition::{PolicyVersion, StateMode};
use wf_domain::retention::RetentionOverride;
use wf_domain::workflow::active::LimitEnforcement;
use wf_domain::workflow::admission::AdmissionLimits;
use wf_domain::workflow::request::RequestScope;
use wf_ports::log::{prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame, verify_complete_policy_replace_frame};
use wf_types::identity::{GroupId, RecoveryId, RequestId, TenantId};
use wf_types::version::{CommittedTime, HlcTimestamp};

use super::super::{PRESENT_INTENT_BYTES, TestResult, minimal_data, present_data, profile};
use super::literals::{assert_replace_frame_list_order, replace_frame_literal};

pub(super) fn replace_frame_input(
    data: CompletePolicyData,
    guard: Option<u64>,
    ids: [&[u8]; 4],
    stamp: CommittedTime,
) -> TestResult<CompletePolicyReplaceInput> {
    Ok(CompletePolicyReplaceInput::new(
        RequestScope::new(
            TenantId::new(ids[0].to_vec())?,
            GroupId::new(ids[1].to_vec())?,
            RecoveryId::new(ids[2].to_vec())?,
        ),
        RequestId::new(ids[3].to_vec())?,
        stamp,
        guard,
        data,
    ))
}

pub(super) fn replace_frame_empty_field(
    data: &mut CompletePolicyData,
    case: usize,
    present: bool,
) -> TestResult {
    let retry = data.retry.as_mut().ok_or("retry fixture")?;
    let state = data
        .states
        .get_mut(b"s".as_slice())
        .ok_or("state fixture")?;
    let governance = data.governance.as_mut().ok_or("governance fixture")?;
    let effects = governance.effects.as_mut().ok_or("effects fixture")?;
    let approvals = governance.approvals.as_mut().ok_or("approvals fixture")?;
    match case {
        0 => data.version = present.then(|| PolicyVersion::Bytes(Vec::new())),
        1 => retry.exhausted_to = present.then(Vec::new),
        2 => data.indexed_state_meta = present.then(Vec::new),
        3 => {
            governance
                .budgets
                .as_mut()
                .and_then(|rules| rules.get_mut(b"b".as_slice()))
                .ok_or("budget fixture")?
                .unit = present.then(Vec::new)
        }
        4 => data.indexed_attributes = present.then(Vec::new),
        5 => effects.allowed = present.then(Vec::new),
        6 => effects.denied = present.then(Vec::new),
        7 => {
            governance
                .circuits
                .as_mut()
                .and_then(|rules| rules.get_mut(b"c".as_slice()))
                .ok_or("circuit fixture")?
                .error_classes = present.then(Vec::new)
        }
        8 => approvals.effects = present.then(Vec::new),
        9 => approvals.states = present.then(Vec::new),
        10 => approvals.assignees = present.then(Vec::new),
        11 => governance.limits = present.then(BTreeMap::new),
        12 => governance.budgets = present.then(BTreeMap::new),
        13 => governance.circuits = present.then(BTreeMap::new),
        14 => {
            governance.effects = present.then_some(EffectsData {
                allowed: None,
                denied: None,
                require_idempotency_key: None,
            })
        }
        15 => {
            governance.audit = present.then_some(AuditData {
                effect_events: None,
                denials: None,
            })
        }
        16 => {
            governance.approvals = present.then_some(ApprovalsData {
                effects: None,
                states: None,
                assignees: None,
                timeout_ms: None,
            })
        }
        17 => state.retry = present.then(RetryOverride::default),
        18 => state.retention = present.then(RetentionOverride::default),
        19 => {
            state.governance = if present {
                state.governance.take()
            } else {
                None
            }
        }
        20 => data.retry = present.then(RetryOverride::default),
        21 => data.retention = present.then(RetentionOverride::default),
        22 => {
            data.governance = present.then_some(GovernanceData {
                mode: None,
                effects: None,
                audit: None,
                limits: None,
                budgets: None,
                circuits: None,
                approvals: None,
            })
        }
        _ => return Err("unknown independent presence fixture".into()),
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn replace_frame_widths(data: &mut CompletePolicyData, maximum: bool) -> TestResult {
    let scalar = if maximum { u64::MAX } else { 0 };
    data.version = Some(PolicyVersion::Number(scalar));
    data.max_active_ms = Some(scalar);
    let retry = data.retry.as_mut().ok_or("retry fixture")?;
    retry.max_retries = Some(if maximum { u16::MAX } else { 0 });
    let backoff = retry.backoff.as_mut().ok_or("backoff fixture")?;
    backoff.base_ms = scalar;
    backoff.max_ms = scalar;
    backoff.jitter_pct = if maximum { 255 } else { 0 };
    data.retention = Some(RetentionOverride {
        ttl_ms: Some(scalar),
        history_max_events: Some(if maximum { u32::MAX } else { 0 }),
    });
    let state = data
        .states
        .get_mut(b"s".as_slice())
        .ok_or("state fixture")?;
    state.mode = Some(if maximum {
        StateMode::Fifo
    } else {
        StateMode::Parallel
    });
    state.retention = data.retention;
    let governance = data.governance.as_mut().ok_or("governance fixture")?;
    governance
        .effects
        .as_mut()
        .ok_or("effects fixture")?
        .require_idempotency_key = Some(maximum);
    governance.mode = Some(if maximum {
        GovernanceMode::Full
    } else {
        GovernanceMode::Minimal
    });
    governance.audit = Some(AuditData {
        effect_events: Some(maximum),
        denials: Some(if maximum {
            DenialAuditMode::All
        } else {
            DenialAuditMode::Off
        }),
    });
    let limit = governance

        9 => {

pub(super) fn assert_replace_frame_duplicate_priority() -> TestResult {
    for (maximum, frame_cap, expected_g, expected_p, error) in [
        (
            2_967,
            149,
            2_839,
            128,
            CompletePolicyEncodingError::Malformed,
        ),
        (
            2_966,
            149,
            2_710,
            128,
            CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(PolicySchemaError::WorkBytes {
                bytes: 2_967,
                maximum: 2_966,
            }),
        ),
        (2_325, 148, 2_325, 0, CompletePolicyEncodingError::ByteLimit),
        (
            2_708,
            149,
            2_453,
            0,
            CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(PolicySchemaError::WorkBytes {
                bytes: 2_709,
                maximum: 2_708,
            }),
        ),
    ] {
        let limits = profile(maximum)?;
        let mut charge = PolicySchemaCharge::new(limits);
        let mut data = minimal_data();
        data.indexed_attributes = Some(vec![b"a".to_vec(), b"a".to_vec()]);
        let result = prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            super::super::input(data, None)?,
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::new(1_048_576, frame_cap, 1_000)?,
            &mut charge,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            result.err().ok_or("exact duplicate priority")?,
            CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(error)
        );
        assert_eq!((charge.g(), charge.p()), (expected_g, expected_p));
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn replace_frame_hex(hex: &str) -> TestResult<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    for pair in hex.as_bytes().as_chunks::<2>().0 {
        bytes.push(u8::from_str_radix(std::str::from_utf8(pair)?, 16)?);
    }
    assert_eq!(bytes.len() * 2, hex.len());
    Ok(bytes)
}

pub(super) fn replace_frame_literal(
    intent: &[u8],
    ids: [&[u8]; 4],
    stamp: CommittedTime,
) -> TestResult<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut expected = b"FWCP\0\x01\x06".to_vec();
    for id in ids {
        expected.extend_from_slice(&u32::try_from(id.len())?.to_be_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(id);
    }
    expected.extend_from_slice(b"\0\x02");
    expected.extend_from_slice(&<[u8; 32]>::from(Sha256::digest(intent)));
    expected.extend_from_slice(&stamp.hlc().physical().get().to_be_bytes());
    expected.extend_from_slice(&stamp.hlc().logical().to_be_bytes());
    expected.extend_from_slice(&stamp.wall().get().to_be_bytes());
    expected.extend_from_slice(&u32::try_from(intent.len())?.to_be_bytes());
    expected.extend_from_slice(intent);
    Ok(expected)
}

pub(super) fn assert_replace_frame_verified(
    verified: &VerifiedCompletePolicyReplaceFrame<'_>,
    expected: &[u8],
    log: LogIdentity,
) {
    let mut cursor = 7;
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    let mut scope = b"FWSC\0\x01".to_vec();
    for index in 0..4 {
        assert_eq!(&expected[cursor..cursor + 2], &[0, 0]);
        let length = usize::from(u16::from_be_bytes(
            expected[cursor + 2..cursor + 4].as_chunks::<2>().0[0],
        ));
        if index < 3 {
            scope.extend_from_slice(&expected[cursor..cursor + 4]);
        }
        cursor += 4;
        ids.push(&expected[cursor..cursor + length]);
        if index < 3 {
            scope.extend_from_slice(ids[index]);
        }
        cursor += length;
    }
    let original = &expected[cursor + 56..];
    let digest = PreparedDigest::new(Sha256::digest(expected).into());
    let intent: [u8; 32] = Sha256::digest(original).into();
    let physical = u64::from_be_bytes(expected[cursor + 34..cursor + 42].as_chunks::<8>().0[0]);
    let logical = u16::from_be_bytes(expected[cursor + 42..cursor + 44].as_chunks::<2>().0[0]);
    let wall = u64::from_be_bytes(expected[cursor + 44..cursor + 52].as_chunks::<8>().0[0]);
    let header = verified.header(log);
    assert_eq!(verified.encoded(), expected);
    assert_eq!(verified.original_intent(), original);
    assert_eq!(verified.digest(), digest);
    assert_eq!(verified.isolation_scope(), scope);
    assert_eq!(header.format_version, 1);
    assert_eq!(header.scope.tenant().as_bytes(), ids[0]);
    assert_eq!(header.scope.group().as_bytes(), ids[1]);
    assert_eq!(header.scope.recovery().as_bytes(), ids[2]);
    assert_eq!(header.request.as_bytes(), ids[3]);
    assert_eq!(header.intent.version(), 2);
    assert_eq!(*header.intent.digest(), intent);
    assert_eq!(header.stamp.hlc().physical().get(), physical);
    assert_eq!(header.stamp.hlc().logical(), logical);
    assert_eq!(header.stamp.wall().get(), wall);
    assert_eq!(header.identity, EntryIdentity::new(log, digest));
    assert_eq!(header.encoded_entry, expected);
    assert_eq!(header.encoded_isolation_scope, scope);
}

pub(super) fn assert_replace_frame_account(
    maximum: u64,

) -> TestResult {

    };

    let mut produced = Vec::new();
    let mut verified = Vec::new();
    let fee = if producer { 4_612 } else { 4_423 };
    let attempts = if repeated { 2 } else { 1 };
    let initial = if held_peak { 1_928 } else { 0 };
    let peak = if held_peak { 64 } else { 0 };
    assert_eq!((charge.g(), charge.p()), (initial, peak));
    for attempt in 1..=attempts {
        let target = initial + fee * attempt + peak;
        let result = if producer {
            prepare_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                super::super::input(minimal_data(), None)?,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                &mut charge,
            )
            .map(|value| produced.push(value))
        } else {
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(

                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),

            )

        };
        if maximum < target {
            assert_eq!(
                result,
                Err(CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(
                    CompletePolicyEncodingError::Schema(PolicySchemaError::WorkBytes {
                        bytes: target,
                        maximum
                    })
                ))
            );
            assert_eq!(
                (charge.g(), charge.p(), charge.total()),
                (target - peak - 263, peak, target - 263)
            );
        } else {
            result?;
            assert_eq!(
                (charge.g(), charge.p(), charge.total()),
                (target - peak, peak, target)
            );
        }
    }
    for value in &produced {
        assert_eq!(value.as_bytes(), expected);
        assert_eq!(
            value.digest(),
            PreparedDigest::new(Sha256::digest(&expected).into())
        );
    }
    for value in &verified {
        assert_replace_frame_verified(
            value,
            &expected,
            LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
        );
    }
    if let Some(seed) = seed {
        let mut expected = minimal_data();
        expected.indexed_attributes = Some(vec![b"a".to_vec()]);
        assert!(seed.data() == &expected);
        assert_eq!(seed.generation(), 1);
    }
    assert_eq!(charge.p(), peak);
    Ok(())
}

    assert_eq!(
        verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(&bytes, limits, AdmissionLimits::default(), charge)
            .err()
            .ok_or("digest mismatch")?,
        CompletePolicyRequestError::IntentMismatch

    for (declared, error) in [
        (51_u32, CompletePolicyEncodingError::TrailingBytes),
        (53, CompletePolicyEncodingError::Malformed),
        (1_048_577, CompletePolicyEncodingError::ByteLimit),
    ] {
        let mut bytes = minimum.clone();

pub(super) fn assert_replace_frame_tags(
    limits: PolicySchemaLimits,
    charge: &mut PolicySchemaCharge,
) -> TestResult {
    let minimum = replace_frame_hex(FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES[0].0)?;
    for (offset, value, error) in [
        (0, b'X', CompletePolicyEncodingError::Malformed),
        (5, 2, CompletePolicyEncodingError::UnsupportedVersion),
        (6, 5, CompletePolicyEncodingError::UnsupportedTag),
        (28, 1, CompletePolicyEncodingError::UnsupportedVersion),
        (83, b'X', CompletePolicyEncodingError::Malformed),
        (118, 2, CompletePolicyEncodingError::InvalidOptionality),
        (124, 2, CompletePolicyEncodingError::InvalidOptionality),
    ] {
        let mut bytes = minimum.clone();
        bytes[offset] = value;
        let result = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
            &bytes,
            limits,
            AdmissionLimits::default(),
            charge,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            result.err().ok_or("malformed mutation")?,
            CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(error)
        );
    }
    let mut full = replace_frame_hex(FROZEN_COMPLETE_REPLACE_FRAMES[1].0)?;
    for (offset, value) in [
        (42, 2),
        (65, 4),
        (114, 2),
        (165, 3),
        (188, 2),
        (191, 2),
        (193, 3),
        (213, 2),
        (250, 2),
    ] {
        let previous = full[83 + offset];
        full[83 + offset] = value;
        let result =
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(&full, limits, AdmissionLimits::default(), charge);
        assert_eq!(
            result.err().ok_or("enum precedes stale digest")?,
            CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::UnsupportedTag)
        );
        full[83 + offset] = previous;
    }
    for start in [61, 71] {
        let mut bytes = minimum.clone();
        bytes[start..start + 8].copy_from_slice(&u64::MAX.to_be_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                &bytes,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge
            )
            .err()
            .ok_or("invalid trusted stamp")?,
            CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::Malformed)
        );
    }
    let stamp = CommittedTime::new(HlcTimestamp::new(0, 0)?, 0)?;
    for field in 1..4 {
        for length in [256, 257] {
            let id = vec![b'x'; length];
            let mut ids = [&b"t"[..], &b"g"[..], &b"r"[..], &b"q"[..]];
            ids[field] = &id;
            let expected = replace_frame_literal(MINIMAL_INTENT_BYTES, ids, stamp)?;
            let result = verify_complete_policy_replace_frame(
                &expected,
                limits,
                AdmissionLimits::default(),
                charge,
            );
            if length == 257 {
                assert_eq!(
                    result.err().ok_or("ID RAW +1")?,
                    CompletePolicyRequestError::Encoding(CompletePolicyEncodingError::ByteLimit)
                );
            } else {
                assert_replace_frame_verified(
                    &result?,
                    &expected,
                    LogIdentity::new(1, 2, AppliedPosition::new(3)),
                );
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

## DOC-NEXT-M1-POLICY-RETENTION-INGRESS1 (2026-10-15; finite proposal only)

Recommend the original RETENTION OVERRIDE normalizer plus its exact captured-limit diagnostics as the next coherent pure M1 component. I read pinned66586c5 RetryPolicy25–59,62–130,290–321,569–577,617–708,746–828,831–919,964–974; the actual Retention module is cleanup/I/O and is not the normalizer. I also read current retention.rs, completed retry_input, CONTENT1/rejection encoder, implementation-plan/CONTINUE/ADR006 and the mandatory source clauses below. There is NO standalone full-default retention normalizer in that source: full normalize_flow_policy calls the same optional override function, and resolve_retention separately merges captured/default/type/state/command values and caps. Do not invent a new full-default API or silently fill absent fields. This recommendation is separate from the frozen retry source review and Root's532+4 source-stage result/online RustSec DNS failure. Existing code/tests remain untouched.

Concrete minimal proposed inventory: ONE NEW production crates/wf-domain/src/policy/complete/retention_input.rs, TWO NEW existing-target tests crates/wf-domain/tests/complete_policy/retention_input.rs and retention_input/refusals.rs; existing complete.rs gains private mod retention_input and exactly the three public names below; testmain gains only literal "\nmod retention_input;\n" (22 B). ROOT's existing codec_policy/original_policy.rs gains ONE function original_retention_input_stays_pure_and_server_side, covering the new descendant, pure/env/async/M0 exclusions and the three exports against client/wire/domain-value forwarding; no checker path/module/dependency/config exception is needed. Production≤400/test-tooling≤600/functions≤100 remain ordinary hard limits. Routine private helper functions within these responsibilities need no inert-body/helper approval loop, but a genuinely new alias/model/path requires consultation before creation.

REUSE existing RawPolicyRetryValue<'input> and OriginalPolicyMapKey<'input> unchanged rather than invent an identical second raw-value graph. All seven existing classes (Nil,Integer(i128),Atom,Binary,Map,Keyword,Other) faithfully cover every reached retention class: out-of-i128 integers and unsupported scalar classes reject at either positive numeric field, while unknown fields remain semantically ignored. Atom("nil") is the nil value alias but retains its3 represented bytes; key Atom("nil") remains an unknown key. Keyword means already-classified proper atom-key pairs, Map supplied captured entries, and Other hides unrepresented source payload/identity. Raw syntax/ETF/safety/hidden bytes/full map uniqueness are not certified. The existing retry-named type remains backward compatible and its documentation is not broadened into a generic term-parser promise. The NEW retention API documents this deliberate shared descriptor vocabulary.

Exact shared PRIVATE seam proposed in the same decision: keep retry_input/value.rs private; change ONLY existing value::select visibility from pub(super) to pub(in crate::policy::complete), and add pub(super) use value::select in existing retry_input.rs. The retention sibling calls retry_input::select(raw,name,samecharge). Its current function BODY and ALL old public APIs/results/events remain byte-exact; no renamed selector, generic public debit/credit/accepted token or new adapter trait/model is introduced. This reuses the actual fresh paid atom-preference/last-Keyword selector rather than copying Map.new into a heap or inventing uncharged descriptor traversal. Retention owns its own three-name paid preflight/mask; the existing eight-name retry preflight and all old retry tariffs stay unchanged. 1. Boundary, identity and comparator. Keep the LOWER replace=true allocator boundary, binary policy_key, raw expected and raw patch, not public Policy.set option preprocessing. Choose the private injective canonical rank Integer < Atom < Binary < Tuple < List < Map. This is registry3's injective order, not Erlang term order. Nil has Atom rank and canonical bytes "nil", though its compact wire tag is0. Each recursive compare admits PAIR128 BEFORE reading classes. Different classes stop then. Same Atom/Binary admits128+both canonical byte lengths before exact comparison. Any new unbounded magnitude walk receives a fresh explicit charge. Atom access borrows already-validated UTF-8 bytes and cannot hide another UTF-8 scan.

Tuple compares arity under PAIR128, then elements recursively. List compares logical heads sequentially and the ACTUAL terminal term; empty proper List sorts before a nonempty List. Each followed raw tail chunk pays128 before access. Proper/improper fragmentation is canonicalized without a temporary list Vec; list-valued ELEMENTS are never flattened. A raw ImproperList whose prefix is empty is Malformed. Its final nonlist terminal may be Nil atom and remains improper. Map compares pair count, then canonical key/value pairs recursively. Raw map ordering prepares one active region: container128, then each raw row read128 and compact slot placement128. Adjacent sorted keys receive a fresh exact comparison; equality is operational Malformed before any frame escapes. Parent raw map cursor/start/len live on the bounded recursion stack. Regions are LIFO/checkpointed and never clobber ancestors. Active regions refer to disjoint raw row OCCURRENCES under both operands and ancestors; aliased pointers are counted again as occurrences in preflight, and no occurrence is staged twice concurrently. 2. Exact grammar. All u32 fields are big-endian. Every node starts u32 node_len INCLUDING that four-byte prefix, then tag. Canonical tags:
0 Nil atom: total5, no payload.
1 Integer: total10+L, sign:u8 (0 or1), L:u32, significant little-endian magnitude[L]. Zero is sign0/L0. High zero padding and negative zero are noncanonical on wire.
2 Atom /3 Binary: total9+L, L:u32, bytes[L]. Atom bytes are UTF-8; Atom("nil") MUST use tag0. Binary is opaque.
4 Map: total17+8*p+sum(child lengths), map_id:u32, pair_count p:u32, (2*p+1) child offsets:u32, then canonical key/value children. Offsets are relative NODESTART, first17+8*p, last=node_len.
5 proper List /6 Tuple: total13+4*n+sum(child lengths), count n:u32, (n+1) offsets:u32, then children; first13+4*n and last=node_len. Empty proper List is tag5/count0/offset13, NEVER Nil tag0.
7 improper list: prefix_count p>=1, (p+2) offsets for p prefix children plus one actual terminal node. First17+4*p, last=node_len. Canonical terminal is neither List nor ImproperList, because proper chunks are concatenated. Total is17+4*p+sum(prefix and terminal node lengths).
8 is RESERVED and returns operational UnsupportedTag, not caller rejection or source corruption.

All count/length/offset arithmetic is checked; offsets have exact contiguous coverage, no gaps/overlap/alternate child bounds/trailing bytes. Canonical count/depth/text bounds apply to scanned nodes as well as producer occurrences. Raw Integer/Big aliases produce ONE significant representation; raw list chunks produce ONE logical list representation. The represented semantic classes and their distinctions do not depend on physical tag choice.

Map IDs are GLOBAL CANONICAL PREORDER over expected first, then patch. They are never assigned in captured/source preorder. Canonical traversal of nested keys/values fixes IDs independently of input map permutation. Sidecar records follow those IDs. A sidecar is: M:u32; (M+1) record_offsets:u32 relative SIDECARSTART; then M records. First offset8+4*M, last=S. Record i is map_node_offset:u32 RELATIVE INTENTSTART, pair_count:u32, pair_count ranks:u32; record width8+4*p. ranks[source_ordinal]=canonical_row_ordinal, each exactly once in0..p. Therefore S=8+12*M+4*sum(p). MapID/record index, map offset, node pair count and exact record range must agree. Empty maps STILL get an ID and empty record. Strict owner-free permutation checks pay4 before each rank read and16 before each earlier-rank equality check; no validation bitmap owner. Source order is used ONLY by Fresh/business cursor; canonical comparison ignores this sidecar.

+fn assert_raw(actual: RawFlowPolicyValue<'_>, expected: RawFlowPolicyValue<'_>) {
+    match (actual, expected) {
+        (RawFlowPolicyValue::Nil, RawFlowPolicyValue::Nil)
+        | (RawFlowPolicyValue::Other, RawFlowPolicyValue::Other) => {}
+        (RawFlowPolicyValue::Integer(a), RawFlowPolicyValue::Integer(b)) => assert_eq!(a, b),
+        (RawFlowPolicyValue::Atom(a), RawFlowPolicyValue::Atom(b)) => assert_eq!(a, b),
+        (RawFlowPolicyValue::Binary(a), RawFlowPolicyValue::Binary(b)) => assert_eq!(a, b),
+        (
+            RawFlowPolicyValue::BigInteger {
+                negative: a,
+                little_endian: aa,
+            },
+            RawFlowPolicyValue::BigInteger {
+                negative: b,
+                little_endian: bb,
+            },
+        ) => {
+            assert_eq!(a, b);
+            assert_eq!(aa, bb);
+        }
+        (RawFlowPolicyValue::Map(a), RawFlowPolicyValue::Map(b)) => {
+            assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
+            for ((ak, av), (bk, bv)) in a.iter().zip(b) {
+                assert_raw(*ak, *bk);
+                assert_raw(*av, *bv);
+            }
+        }
+        (RawFlowPolicyValue::List(a), RawFlowPolicyValue::List(b))
+        | (RawFlowPolicyValue::Tuple(a), RawFlowPolicyValue::Tuple(b)) => {
+            assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
+            for (a, b) in a.iter().zip(b) {
+                assert_raw(*a, *b);
+            }
+        }
+        (
+            RawFlowPolicyValue::ImproperList {
+                prefix: a,
+                tail: aa,
+            },
+            RawFlowPolicyValue::ImproperList {
+                prefix: b,
+                tail: bb,
+            },
+        ) => {
+            assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
+            for (a, b) in a.iter().zip(b) {
+                assert_raw(*a, *b);
+            }
+            assert_raw(*aa, *bb);
+        }
+        other => panic!("different original terms: {other:?}"),
+    }
 }

## DOMAIN-NEXT-M1-ORIGINAL-PUBLIC-REPLY1-PROPOSE1 — concrete generic owner and joint inventory

PROPOSED, not creation authority. Root chose GENERIC decoder-accepted projection, not a normalized-lower-only subset. This is the initial concrete inventory for one ARCH decision; the finite primitive schedules and representative decimals below remain ordinary pre-RED work where marked OPEN. No new source/test/module/model has been created. The preceding merge component is reviewed and committed asf1fc232; its registry4 frame, retained original-envelope responses, bytes and fees remain exact.

The source boundary is the real public CALLER after a successful Router binary response, or after an original Policy.get read. A fresh structural retained-index decode is faithful to Policy.do_set itself; it is not a second policy business admission or an artificial encode/parse adapter. Setter projection does NOT bind decoded atom:type to the requested type. Getter projection DOES bind it; absent get returns generation0/default projection without synthetic ETF. Router error results bypass this successful-binary projector and stay forwarded by their existing caller. The new component does not repurpose registry4 retained response bytes as already-projected replies or add another verifier/gate.

All decoded safe-map fields remain generic. Version is ANY raw term. Max-active is ANY signed integer, including negative and arbitrarily wide Big; other classes present nil. Retry outer maps replace ANY max_retries/exhausted_to values, and exact-key Map.merge of backoff preserves unknown keys and values. Retention preserves raw ttl/history fields without applying business/C caps. Source hot-min is total and its result is deleted, so the NEW reply schedule may omit that dead comparison/value while retaining defaults and every reached retention Enumerable/struct guard. Captured caller defaults use resolve_retention/3 semantics, not ApplyContext/history admission. A configured hot default can affect captured default history before this component, so it cannot simply be ignored at capture.

All-state rows expose ANY state governance value directly; selected uses Elixir ||, falling back ONLY for false/nil (empty list/map, zero and other values are truthy). Type governance remains map-only. States LIST is Map.new enumerable but is NOT consulted by state_mode/state_retry/state_retention/state_governance, which require a MAP; list row config is ignored. Every valid list callback runs before LAST duplicate collapse; malformed tuples or improper terminals refuse at the actual reached point, including after successful callbacks. Struct dispatch remains reached-only: retry/retention Enum.reduce and all-state Map.new can require unsupported/custom Enumerable; backoff Map.merge treats struct-shaped maps as ordinary maps. Full VM/custom Enumerable/capture and original physical/setup/profile/Linux obligations remain REQUIRED.

Representation: one public semantic owner borrows original encoded payload, requested type/query and safety/capture donors under ONE explicit common input lifetime. It owns one retained original index/catalog and bounded reply metadata; it does not clone a whole term AST or emit a projected ETF Vec. Common lifetime is the intersection of those donor lifetimes, not a claim that the owner outlives their bytes/tables. Input descriptor structs may drop; raw/safety/query payload owners must remain. Every actual term view is created from &owner, using stored existing TermPosition or compact synthetic references. No field stores a cursor borrowing its own owner. Float, bits, runtime and other source terms retain exact encoded views rather than a unit Other identity certificate.

Persistent sharing is mandatory: fixed default/type retry and backoff bases are computed ONCE. ## M2-STATE-CONTRACT1 PROPOSAL — neutral transaction and core values only

READ-ONLY candidate for named ARCH selection, NOT creation/release. Root618/70+4 and the final batch sources are closed with the exact default-DNS/cached-audit qualifications above; I actually whole-read final ARCH8909/f44c2e53 and PERF6145/ba5a5240. The five literal pure M1 model subjects are met, not full original/native parity. Current backend readiness is different: wf-storage/log,state,transaction,snapshot and wf-consensus/adapter,apply,membership,read are empty stubs. No engine or OpenRaft dependency is adopted. Root's redb acquisition failed DNS and its source/cache is absent. No cached-engine substitution, in-memory production backend or fake crash proof is proposed.

Smallest useful next batch: specify the semantic ordered transaction and independently round-trip the core/control/record-batch5 values that a real engine must persist. Keep codecs in STORAGE, effect capability in PORTS, no OpenRaft/redb types inward. This prerequisite does NOT claim atomicity, crash recovery, a live state machine or storage-v2 conformance. The real engine transaction + child-process termination tests remain the next mandatory gate once acquisition/release selection is possible.

Exact proposed production inventory (five NEW files):
1 crates/wf-ports/src/state/transaction.rs — semantic capabilities/models below, no implementation/backend handle.
2 crates/wf-storage/src/state/value.rs — closed value facade, StateValueError, bounded byte navigation/building, no filesystem.
3 crates/wf-storage/src/state/value/control.rs — exact group-control value grammar.
4 crates/wf-storage/src/state/value/record.rs — existing core record+ordering grammar/restoration.
5 crates/wf-storage/src/state/value/outcome.rs — exact record-batch5 retained owner grammar.
Existing seams: ports/state.rs and storage/state.rs register/reexport selected surfaces; workflow.rs adds latest_event_witness()->(EventKind,u64,Fence); workflow/control.rs adds last_entry_stamp()->Option<EntryStamp>. Both getters are immutable facts, no new witness type or inferred provenance. Root owns shared registrations/checker/docs/ledger/Git; Writer owns the five substantive files and domain getter bodies if selected; Root may own disjoint tests. No Cargo/dependency/OpenRaft/unsafe changes in this prerequisite.

Named public models: GroupApplyStore trait; GroupApplyTransaction trait; GroupDueCursor trait; DueCursorStep<'row> enum; StoredWorkflowRecord struct; GroupApplyChanges<'scope,'view> sealed-field struct; StateTransactionError enum; StateValueError enum. Reuse existing typed identities/control/domain plans and existing AdmissionLimits; no extra general raw-KV, backend transaction wrapper, policy schema or memory-store model. StoredWorkflowRecord contains tenant, partition, WorkflowRecord and OrderingMetadata. The group+recovery is bound by the transaction/codec arguments, never independently advanced per tenant.

Proposed effect signatures (associated concrete guards remain backend-private; no backend API is exported):
- GroupApplyStore::begin_apply<'s>(&'s mut self, group:&GroupId, recovery:&RecoveryId, maximum_read_rows:usize, maximum_read_bytes:usize) -> Result<Self::Transaction<'s>,StateTransactionError>.
- GroupApplyTransaction has an associated DueCursor<'tx>:GroupDueCursor. control()->Result<ControlState,...>; outcome(tenant:&TenantId,request:&RequestId)->Result<Option<RetainedOutcome>,...>; record(tenant,partition,id)->Result<Option<StoredWorkflowRecord>,...>; parallel_member(tenant,due:DueOrder<'_>)->Result<bool,...>; fifo_member(tenant,lane:LaneKey<'_>,member:LaneOrder<'_>)->Result<Option<StoredWorkflowRecord>,...>; fifo_head(tenant,lane)->Result<Option<StoredWorkflowRecord>,...>.
- due_cursor<'tx>(&'tx mut self, tenant:&TenantId, query:ClaimQuery<'_>, after:Option<DueOrder<'_>>, maximum_rows:usize, maximum_bytes:usize)->Result<Self::DueCursor<'tx>,...>. Query fields are semantic existing values, never storage keys.
- GroupDueCursor::next(&mut self)->Result<DueCursorStep<'_>,...>; position(&self)->Option<DueOrder<'_>>. Step is Row(DueOrder<'row>), RangeEnd or BudgetEnd. Row/position borrow the cursor and cannot survive advance/drop. Continuation is an advisory semantic position, freshly revalidated if reopened; BudgetEnd is NEVER proof of no eligible work. An actual cursor is a prefix of the requested committed index order, not a sorted arbitrary candidate window.
- commit(self, changes:&GroupApplyChanges<'_, '_>)->Result<(),StateTransactionError> CONSUMES the transaction. All methods are synchronous effect ports; no I/O callback enters the domain.

One ordered writer/guard and one authoritative revision span every point/membership/head/range read, pure decision and consumed commit. Backend read guards never escape into domain objects. Every returned row binds the requested tenant/group/recovery/partition/id, canonical ordering and index identity; malformed/mismatched rows are Corrupt, not absent. fifo_head is the ACTUAL first row of that lane under the same transaction; bounded unrelated materialization cannot certify it. Cursor row/byte caps are additionally constrained by the transaction's cumulative remaining read bounds, with no per-page budget reset. Point/head owners are only the consumed keys and true heads; no whole-group clone/read is required. An absent point is an actual transactional observation, never an error fallback.

GroupApplyChanges::new(scope:&RequestScope,expected:ControlState,plan:RecordBatchApplyPlan<'view>)->Result<Self,...> owns the plan, borrows the scope, validates contained Fresh/Replay outcome namespace, and exposes only immutable accessors. At commit the adapter MUST compare group+recovery and exact expected predecessor identity/stamp/control against that SAME guard. Tenant scopes address business/outcome rows; group control/membership remains global. Accepted plan writes exactly touched records/order/index/history + new outcome + next control. Deterministic rejection writes ONLY new rejection outcome+control. Replay/intent-conflict/expired preserve original outcomes and write only processing control; exact LogReplay writes nothing. The plan and read owners stay alive through commit; publication occurs only after success. KnownAborted means durable predecessor unchanged and no publication; Uncertain cannot be recast as known abort or business rejection, fences new writers/reads requiring authority until durable reopen/reconciliation. Corrupt/Unavailable/Limit/Allocation are operational error variants. There is no test-double claim that this contract itself supplies durable success.

Current pure views are borrowed BTreeMaps, NOT a transaction capability. No existing bounded map will be advertised as complete. Joining this protocol to Fresh-only loading will require an explicitly selected outer phase seam (verify/header gate, consumed point/head/range load, existing pure decision) before an engine driver; no double gate and no domain I/O. That driver/seam is deliberately NOT created by this prerequisite. Initial policy/ActiveRecord/membership/physical-index value formats and full public apply profile remain required; unknown profiles fail closed, never default to absent policy/membership.

Closed codec APIs, all in wf-storage::state::value:
encode_control(group,recovery,ControlState,maximum_bytes)->Vec<u8>; decode_control(bytes,expected_group,expected_recovery,maximum_bytes)->ControlState.
encode_record(group,recovery,&StoredWorkflowRecord,AdmissionLimits,maximum_bytes)->Vec<u8>; decode_record(bytes,expected_group,expected_recovery,AdmissionLimits,maximum_bytes)->StoredWorkflowRecord.
encode_outcome(&RetainedOutcome,maximum_bytes)->Vec<u8>; decode_outcome(bytes,expected_scope,expected_request,AdmissionLimits,maximum_bytes)->RetainedOutcome.
All return Result<_,StateValueError>; complete structural bounds precede allocations, checked arithmetic, fallible variable reserves, exact EOF/optionality/version, no serde or native struct bytes. Distinct FWSC/FWSR/FWSO version1 discriminators; explicit BE widths, u32 raw lengths and presence tags, opaque binary IDs including NUL/FF. StateValueError preserves unsupported/malformed/overflow/limit/allocation/invalid-value distinctions as operational values.

Control encodes group+recovery, current group HLC/wall, unapplied versus applied-index0, full last log identity+prepared digest and EXACT last EntryStamp. Max group clocks cannot reconstruct a backward stamped entry. Record encodes all WorkflowRecordData fields INCLUDING latest kind/version/fence, lease/empty optionals and ordering priority/u128 sequence; decoder reuses restore_record and typed identity constructors. Never infer latest kind from current state. Root's separately reproduced generated next_run_at restoration bug/fix is a prerequisite: a valid generated policy due above external MAX_EXACT must round-trip; no blanket external deadline ceiling is introduced by codecs. Root owns restoration.rs/retry_policy_transitions.rs repair, no Writer edit there.

Outcome codec initially supports ONLY intent5 plus Accepted or IndexedRejected and response_version1. It verifies selected exact [0] or closed rejection bytes/status correspondence, scope/request, original full position/time/expiry and digest, then RetainedOutcome::new. Wrong namespace/request, status/body mismatch and every other intent/status family FAIL CLOSED. This does not silently reinterpret original policy/claim outcomes. Actual key-space/order-preserving encoding is outside this batch: DueOrder is reverse priority,due,RAW id,partition,state,type; FIFO is running-score,u128 sequence,RAW id. Length-prefixed/NUL-separated arbitrary-binary keys cannot be assumed to preserve that order.

ports/tests/state_transaction/main.rs + protocol.rs: one RecordingGroupStore and one RecordingGroupTransaction TEST-ONLY fixture, std iterator/cursor fixture as the concrete associated type; records actual requested point/head/range operations and commit order. Explicit contract doubles, NOT an engine or crash test.

Real engine acceptance remains mandatory and unexecuted: one transactional view/commit; child-process kill before/after every persistence boundary; accepted/rejected/outcome/checkpoint all-or-nothing; lost reply and exact retry; uncertain commit reconciliation/reopen; corrupted bytes fail-stop; original same-index speculative rows/registry/value invisible while index8/9 see earlier committed data; crash-safe snapshot staging/membership/log-vote callbacks; Linux AND macOS. M2-STATE-CONTRACT1 finite signature precision BEFORE any selection/code: every transaction READ method, including due_cursor<'tx>, borrows &'tx self rather than &mut self; the exclusive write transaction is acquired once by begin_apply, so point/head reads can coexist with a live range cursor while commit(self,...) remains forbidden by its borrow until cursors drop. The backend may keep cumulative budget/cursor bookkeeping internally; no guard leaves the capability. GroupDueCursor::next still takes &mut cursor, and a returned Row borrow prevents advancing it. Its provisional last-emitted continuation is SUPERSEDED before any tests/code by last FULLY admitted/consumed inspected candidate, including filtered-out candidates. Never advance beyond a candidate whose key, required record or filter admission did not finish. BudgetEnd preserves that consumed position; this avoids reopening the same all-filtered prefix forever. Charges already spent on a refused candidate stay cumulative.

Exact lifetime/budget spelling: begin_apply<'s>(&'s mut self,group:&'s GroupId,recovery:&'s RecoveryId,maximum_read_steps:usize,maximum_read_bytes:usize) borrows its namespace rather than copying it. due_cursor<'tx>(&'tx self,tenant:&'tx TenantId,query:ClaimQuery<'tx>,after:Option<DueOrder<'tx>>,maximum_rows:usize,maximum_bytes:usize) retains only borrowed filters plus backend-private position. Global/local limits are explicit and positive. The local row cap counts returned rows; the global step cap counts every control/point/membership/head/open attempt including misses, every physically inspected candidate BEFORE filtering and actual empty end probe. Latched terminal returns perform no further backend work. Read bytes count control512; each materialized StoredWorkflowRecord or RetainedOutcome512+ALL owned variable fields; each inspected due key128+id/partition/state/type lengths, plus record charge if filtering materializes one. Boolean/miss/empty has no returned-byte owner. Admission precedes owner construction/visible progress; point failures are Limit, range failures BudgetEnd. No refund or per-page reset, and no backend cache/page/queued-I/O/native RSS guarantee.

One NEW pure server-only API in EXISTING ports/log/record_batch/response.rs, wrapped/reexported by existing record_batch.rs/log.rs:
record_batch_retained_status(intent:ClientIntent,response_version:u16,response:&[u8])->Result<RetainedStatus,CodecError>.
It allocates nothing, requires intent5/response1, and parses the existing closed response table exactly. Unknown root/kind/code/detail is UnsupportedTag; truncation/trailing is Malformed; unsupported profile/version is UnsupportedVersion; checked integer conversion failure is LengthOverflow. FWSO serializes response bytes ONCE without a separate typed status. Decode derives status here; encode compares it with owner.status().
